Administrator guide

PRA Remote Mailbox

Version 3.2.0Updated 2026-11-21Nicolas FabertPowerShell 7.5+ (engine and window)Backup before every change

When the on-premises Exchange servers are lost, PRA Remote Mailbox turns the on-premises mailboxes into remote mailboxes, so that every user gets a mailbox in Exchange Online within the hour — and rolls everything back when Exchange is available again. Only Active Directory is changed on-premises, and every change is backed up first.

New here? Start with the [user guide]fPraRemoteMailbox-UserGuide.md): the same tool, one step after the other, with a picture for each step. This guide is the reference.

Important

Files downloaded from the Internet may be blocked by Windows and fail to run. Before using this project, unblock every file in the downloaded folder:

PowerShell
Get-ChildItem "C:\Chemin\Du\Dossier" -Recurse -File -Force | Unblock-File

Replace the example path with the folder where you downloaded or extracted this project.

The Install-Module commands in this documentation use -Force, so they also update or reinstall a module that is already installed. If an older version still conflicts, close every PowerShell window, open a new one (as administrator for -Scope AllUsers), run Uninstall-Module <ModuleName> -AllVersions -Force, then run the Install-Module command again.

What it does
Convert: on-premises mailbox → remote mailbox (AD attributes, licence group, Entra Connect, shared mailbox permissions in Exchange Online).
How to go back
Recover a Convert batch: original AD attributes, licence removed, cloud shared mailboxes removed before the on-premises ones come back.
How it protects
Preview first; a complete, re-read backup of every object before the first write; the first error stops everything.
How it is used
One script, one configuration file, one short batch ID that links the steps together.
Start here

Quick start

  1. 1
    Check the prerequisites
    PowerShell 7.5+ (pwsh), RSAT ActiveDirectory, ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.10.1+, Microsoft.Graph.Authentication and Microsoft.Graph.Users 2.41.1+ (one same version for both), installed for PowerShell 7 (chapter 4).
  2. 2
    Edit the configuration
    config\PraRemoteMailbox.config.psd1: scope, licence group, routing domain, Entra Connect server, tenant (chapter 6).
  3. 3
    Preview
    .\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert — targets and planned AD changes, nothing is written.
  4. 4
    Apply
    .\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Mode Apply — one confirmation, then backup, AD, sync, Exchange Online.
  5. 5
    Keep the batch ID
    The summary prints it (e.g. efb9d60a) with the next command: -Action Recover -Batch efb9d60a rolls the batch back.

Important

Preview is the default. Without -Mode Apply (or with -WhatIf) the tool only reads. With -Mode Apply it asks one confirmation after showing the plan; -Force skips it for unattended runs. No option ever skips a safety check.

Tip

Ready-to-use commands — one user, a whole OU, only the shared mailboxes, a list, the roll-back: chapter 8, recipes 1 to 6.

The window opens with pwsh -STA -File .\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Gui (native Fluent theme). It starts no operation automatically. Version 3.0.0 has offline validation only; no new live-tenant campaign has been performed for this version (the list to replay is in annex B).

Important

Breaking in 3.0.0: PowerShell 7.5 or later is required. Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe) is refused by #Requires before any code runs, and so is PowerShell 7.4 (the tool reads JSON dates as text with ConvertFrom-Json -DateKind, new in 7.5). The 2.2.x releases remain the Windows PowerShell 5.1 version: keep them for a server that cannot have PowerShell 7. Backups, proofs and Finalize packages written by 2.x restore unchanged with 3.0.0 (same formats, annex D), and the files written by 3.0.0 stay readable by 2.2.x.

Part IUnderstand
Chapter 1

Project background

In short: The tool exists because turning mailboxes into remote mailboxes by hand is slow and risky. This chapter says what is lost, what is kept, and why a tool is safer.

The disaster scenario

  • The mailboxes of the organisation are hosted on-premises (Exchange Server, hybrid with Exchange Online).
  • The disaster recovery plan (PRA) covers the loss of the on-premises Exchange servers: mail must work again quickly, without waiting for their reconstruction.
  • Active Directory and Entra Connect are still available: the identities, groups and synchronisation work.
  • The decision is to give every user a new, empty mailbox in Exchange Online and to recreate the access to the shared mailboxes. The content of the lost mailboxes is not migrated by this tool (it comes back from the Exchange recovery, or from a backup product).
  • When Exchange is back, the objects are rolled back to their on-premises state.

Why a tool

Turning an on-premises mailbox into a remote mailbox means rewriting about ten Exchange attributes in AD, per object, in a precise way, for hundreds of objects, under stress. A wrong value or a lost value cannot be recovered without a backup: this happened with the first script (version 1.2.5), whose backup was written after the changes.

Constraint Value
Objects user mailboxes, shared mailboxes (rooms and equipment possible)
Systems changed Active Directory (attributes, licence group), Entra Connect (one sync cycle), Exchange Online (shared mailbox permissions)
Systems NOT needed Exchange on-premises (it is down)
Servers one server (AD + cloud), or two servers: an AD server and an isolated "cloud" server
Traceability backups, journals, logs, transcripts and reports kept for every run
Chapter 2

How it works

In short: Convert backs up, then changes Active Directory, then waits for Entra Connect and Exchange Online. Recover does the same in reverse, from the backup.

Convert

The default flow, on one server (Execution.Phase = 'Both'):

Read AD
scope, attributes, permissions
BackupJSON + CLIXML + SHA-256, re-read
Write AD
remote mailbox, licence group
Syncone Entra Connect cycle
Exchange Online
mailbox, licence, permissions
Step What happens
Preview Every object of the scope is read, checked (it must be an on-premises mailbox) and planned. The console shows what will change.
Exchange Online pre-check (Apply, phase Both) sign-in, every target and every permission holder resolved in Exchange Online — before any AD write.
Backup One private folder Backups\Batch-<id>: the typed values to restore (JSON), every AD value (CLIXML), their SHA-256, then everything is re-read and compared with the plan.
AD changes Per object: current state re-checked, Set-ADUser, AD re-read, licence group, AD re-read. The first error stops the batch.
Entra Connect One Delta cycle, local or on EntraConnect.Server; the tool waits for its end. Before the first AD write the tool proves that the synchronisation is possible for the account that runs it (an authenticated, read-only call to Get-ADSyncScheduler): otherwise the run stops with nothing written. A cycle that fails after the verified AD writes does not fail the run: Pending, exit code 2.
Exchange Online The tool first confirms, for each object, that the Microsoft Entra ID account with its UPN is the account synchronised from this AD object (chapter 3). It then waits (up to Polling.TimeoutMinutes) for the mailboxes and the licences, then grants FullAccess / SendAs / SendOnBehalf on the shared mailboxes and checks each grant.
X500 control For each mailbox that is ready, the tool proves that it carries the X500 addresses recorded by the AD phase (next section). A missing one is a warning; the conversion stays done.

What changes in AD

Attribute User mailbox Shared mailbox
msExchRecipientTypeDetails 1 → 2147483648 (RemoteUserMailbox) 4 → 34359738368 (RemoteSharedMailbox)
msExchRemoteRecipientType → 1 (3 with archive) → 97 (99 with archive)
msExchRecipientDisplayType → -2147483642 → -2147483642
targetAddress → SMTP:alias@tenant.mail.onmicrosoft.com same
proxyAddresses + smtp:alias@tenant.mail.onmicrosoft.com (Recover removes it again and keeps the cloud X500: address, see below) same
homeMDB, homeMTA, msExchHomeServerName, mDBUseDefaults, msExchMailboxGuid cleared cleared
retention tag (extensionAttribute1 by default) → Converted → Converted
licence group added never (a shared mailbox has no licence)

X500 addresses — replies to old messages keep working

Every message, meeting and cached Outlook entry (nickname cache, delegates, meeting organiser) addresses an on-premises mailbox by its legacyExchangeDN (internally an IMCEAEX address). Convert creates a new cloud mailbox. If that mailbox does not carry X500:<legacyExchangeDN> of the on-premises object, and the X500 addresses already in its proxyAddresses (older legacyExchangeDN values from earlier migrations), a reply to an old message, a meeting update or a cached recipient bounces with an IMCEAEX non-delivery report.

The tool proves this, per object, and never writes a cloud address:

  1. AD phase (Convert, phases AD and Both). legacyExchangeDN is read with the other attributes (read only: it is not one of the managed attributes, is never written, restored or modified). The batch records, for each object, the list ExpectedX500: X500:<legacyExchangeDN> when it is not empty, then every X500: entry of the original proxyAddresses. Duplicates are removed (ordinal, ignoring case, on the whole value); each value is kept byte for byte. The preview shows X500 to verify after the conversion: N for each object. The field travels in the batch JSON and in the transfer package, so the cloud server on another machine has it.
  2. Cloud phase (Convert, phases Cloud and Both). When the mailbox is ready (and its licence, and the shared mailbox permissions), the tool reads EmailAddresses of the mailbox in Exchange Online, or the Entra proxyAddresses when Cloud.MailboxCheckVia is Graph, and compares each expected value (ordinal, ignoring case, on the whole value). Exchange Online never lists the LegacyExchangeDN of a mailbox in its own EmailAddresses, although Entra Connect may have written X500:<that value> on premises while the object was still a MailUser: the tool also asks for the mailbox's own LegacyExchangeDN and counts X500:<it> as present (no false warning). While only these addresses are awaited, the log says mailbox ready; X500 addresses not all visible yet, check N of 3, never Not ready yet. All present: X500: N of N present (legacyExchangeDN + older X500). Otherwise it re-reads, at the polling interval, up to three reads in total (the cloud value can lag one synchronisation; there is no long new wait), then writes ONE warning for the object: X500 missing in Exchange Online: <values>. It is a warning, not an error: the conversion stays done. The warning is counted in the run result, the HTML report, the global report (journey of the object) and the Next steps, which give the command to check again after an Entra Connect synchronisation.
  3. Check. -Action Check -Batch <id> (or -Identity <sAMAccountName>, which reads AD) shows the same comparison, read only. An identity given as a UPN has no Active Directory read: the line says so and skips the control.
  4. Old batches. A batch written before 3.1.0 has no ExpectedX500: the control is skipped with the information line expected addresses not available (batch from 3.0.0 or older), never a failure. The field is validated like KeptX500 when the batch is read (only strings starting with X500:, at most 2,000 values of at most 2,048 characters); a changed or invalid field makes the batch refused.

The control runs only when the mailbox check runs (Cloud.CheckMailbox). Recover is unchanged: it keeps the cloud X500 address written back on premises (chapter 3).

Shared mailbox permissions — where they come from

Exchange on-premises is down: the tool cannot ask it (Get-MailboxPermission is not available). It reads the permissions where Exchange keeps a copy in Active Directory, on the account of the shared mailbox itself (default SharedMailbox.PermissionSource = 'AD'):

Right granted in Exchange Online Read in AD (attribute of the shared mailbox account) Written there on-premises by
FullAccess msExchMailboxSecurityDescriptor — Allow entries with the FullAccess right Add-MailboxPermission -AccessRights FullAccess
SendAs nTSecurityDescriptor (the AD permissions of the account) — Allow entries with the extended right Send As Add-ADPermission -ExtendedRights Send-As, or the Exchange admin center
SendOnBehalf publicDelegates Set-Mailbox -GrantSendOnBehalfTo
Read AD
3 attributes of the shared mailbox
Clean upgroups → users, exclusions
Backup
lists of UPNs in the batch
Pre-checkevery holder found in Exchange Online
Grant
once, then re-read
  1. Only explicit Allow entries are kept: inherited entries are ignored. A Deny entry is not reproduced either (Exchange Online is given Allow entries only), but it is reported as a warning under the shared mailbox, with the accounts it refuses; when one of them is granted anyway (directly, or through a group that is expanded to its users), the warning names it: it gets the access in Exchange Online, and the permission must be removed there after the conversion if it has to stay denied.
  2. System and administration accounts are never reproduced: SELF, NT AUTHORITY\…, BUILTIN\…, Domain / Enterprise / Schema Admins, Organization Management, Exchange Trusted Subsystem, Exchange Servers, Exchange Windows Permissions, Managed Availability Servers, Delegated Setup — plus the accounts listed in SharedMailbox.ExcludeTrusteeSamAccountNames (service accounts, for example).
  3. A group is expanded to its users, nested groups included: Exchange Online receives one permission per user (UPN), never the group itself (lab T16). A user added to the group later does not get the access by itself.
  4. An entry that points to an account no longer in AD ("Account Unknown": deleted account, or an account of another domain), or to an account that is neither a user nor a group (a computer, a managed service account, a foreign security principal; a mail contact among the publicDelegates), cannot be granted: it is ignored and reported as a warning — a yellow ▲ line under the shared mailbox, a [WARN] line in the log, the Warnings column of the CSV, and the Warnings tile and card of the HTML report. The run goes on and its exit code does not change. Every other holder must exist in AD with a UPN.
  5. The lists are saved in the backup of the batch (SharedPermissions of each record): the proof of what was granted.
  6. Apply (phase Both): before any AD write, every holder is looked up in Exchange Online. An unknown holder stops the run before AD is changed. A user still on-premises is fine: Entra Connect has synchronised it as a mail user.
  7. When the cloud shared mailbox exists: Add-MailboxPermission (FullAccess, with AutoMapping), Add-RecipientPermission (SendAs), Set-Mailbox -GrantSendOnBehalfTo (SendOnBehalf). A permission already present is only verified; a missing one is granted once, then re-read until Exchange Online shows it. In a hybrid organisation, Entra Connect usually brings publicDelegates along with the mailbox: SendOnBehalf is then already there and only verified (lab T16).

How to check before the Apply: the preview prints, under each shared mailbox, FullAccess to, SendAs to and SendOnBehalf to with the first holders; the log of the run has the complete lists (lines PERMISSIONS | …). After the Apply, every grant is printed and the report shows Permissions verified=6/6.

Other sources, when the AD entries are not reliable:

PermissionSource Holders
'Csv' file SharedMailbox.CsvPath, columns Shared,Group (see config\SharedPermissions.sample.csv): the members of Group get FullAccess and SendAs on Shared
'CustomAttribute' the AD group whose SharedMailbox.CustomAttribute (e.g. extensionAttribute5) contains the name of the shared mailbox: its members get FullAccess and SendAs
'None' no FullAccess / SendAs

SendOnBehalf always comes from publicDelegates (set CaptureSendOnBehalf = $false to skip it). A Recover does not remove the cloud permissions one by one: they disappear with the cloud mailbox; Convert never changes the on-premises permissions.

Recover

The way back, from the Convert batch:

Convert batch
original values
ADusers restored, shared → MailUser
Exchange Online
mailboxes gone?
Final restoreshared + tags
Done
on-premises again
  • Users get their original attributes back and leave the licence group (unless they were already members before Convert).
  • Shared mailboxes are first deprovisioned in Exchange Online (msExchRemoteRecipientType 8, MailUser): their on-premises attributes come back only when Exchange Online confirms that the cloud mailbox is gone. Otherwise two mailboxes would exist for the same object.
  • The retention tag keeps the value Converted until the cloud check, then gets its original value back.
  • Before anything is changed, the Recover looks at what it is about to overwrite and at what it is about to remove:
    • An object whose managed attributes are neither in the state the Convert left them in nor in their original state (an address added during the disaster, a later Convert of the same object) is named in a warning in the Preview and the Apply: the saved values are put back over what is there now, and the confirmation question says how many objects are concerned. The X500: addresses that the hybrid writeback adds are not a difference.
    • Each mailbox that carries the retention tag must be held by the retention policy in Exchange Online. When one is not, or when that cannot be checked, the Apply stops before any change, with the reason and the commands to go on. The Preview shows the same answer as warnings and says that the Apply will be refused. -AcceptRetentionRisk (a checkbox in the console) goes on for one run, and the configuration file can turn the check off (Retention in chapter 6).
  • On two servers, the cloud server writes a Finalize package that the AD server applies (-Action Finalize).

The four actions

Action Purpose Writes
Convert on-premises mailbox → remote mailbox AD, Entra Connect, Exchange Online permissions
Recover roll back a Convert batch AD, Entra Connect
Finalize last step of a Recover on two servers AD, Entra Connect
Check is a mailbox provisioned / deprovisioned / retained? nothing
Chapter 3

Things to know

In short: The backups are the only way back, the new cloud mailboxes are empty, and the first error stops everything.

Warning

The backups are the only way back. A Recover restores what the Convert batch saved — nothing else. Keep the Backups folder on a durable, protected volume and copy it outside the server after each Apply. Never edit a backup: every file is checked by SHA-256 and a changed file is refused.

Caution

Convert creates new, empty mailboxes in Exchange Online (msExchMailboxGuid is cleared). The content of the on-premises mailboxes is not moved. A Recover deprovisions the cloud mailboxes: mail received in the cloud during the disaster must be exported first if it has to be kept (or protected by a retention policy, see Retention in chapter 6).

What the lab showed after a deprovisioning: Exchange Online keeps the cloud mailbox disconnected (it is not listed as a soft-deleted mailbox), and a new Convert a few minutes later reattached it with the same ExchangeGuid. How long Exchange Online keeps it is not known, so saving its content before a rollback stays the advice. In Exchange Online, the synchronised mail user can have its object id as its Name: search by UPN, alias or address, never by Name.

The cloud X500 address is kept. While an object is a remote mailbox, Entra Connect (Exchange hybrid writeback) adds an X500: address of the cloud mailbox to proxyAddresses and sets msDS-ExternalDirectoryObjectId. A Recover restores proxyAddresses as captured before the Convert plus every X500: address that is on the object at that moment and was not in the original list: nothing else is kept, the routing smtp: address added by Convert is still removed, no X500: is invented, and an address that was already original is not duplicated. Without it, a reply to a message sent from the cloud during the disaster, or a cached Outlook address, would bounce after the rollback. The Preview says N cloud X500 address(es) kept, and the batch records the list (KeptX500; a batch written before 3.0.0 has none).

Note

Nothing is automatic after an error. The first error stops the batch: no next object, no sync, no cloud write, and no automatic rollback. The journal of the batch (Journal-<id>.jsonl) says exactly which write was started, applied and verified. The objects converted and verified before the error keep their AD proof: the State file is written for them and marked partial (it says how many objects were planned). The objects that were not reached are Pending, never skipped. The Next steps give the exact commands: continue the converted objects (-Phase AD -Batch <id>, then -Phase Cloud -Batch <id> for the Exchange Online part), convert the others (fix the cause, then run a new Convert for those objects only: a converted object is refused by the same command, "already converted by batch ...", so with -CsvPath list only the others), or roll the whole batch back (-Action Recover -Batch <id>, Preview first). Once the AD changes are made, a Convert is not run again for the converted objects (see Exit codes). A run that is stopped from outside (Ctrl+C, a closed console, a stop of the host) ends the same way: RESULT: FAIL, exit code 1, the stop named in the summary and the command that goes on, never PASS. When the stop came after Active Directory was changed, the Next steps count the objects that were really verified: if all of them were, they give the continuation (-Action Convert -Phase AD -Batch <id>: the verified objects are not changed again, it runs the synchronisation and writes the package) and the rollback; if not, only the rollback. A backup folder that a run left behind before its first AD write (no State file and no journal line of a write, or marked NOT-APPLIED) is not a batch to roll back: the console lists it as "Nothing was written to AD: nothing to roll back, not a batch to continue", and Recover -Batch refuses it before any change and says so. The exit code is given to the process only when the run is the entry of its own PowerShell process (pwsh -File, -Command, the console's child process): a command typed in an interactive window never closes that window. When every object of a batch was verified and the run stopped before the end, the AD proof written is the normal one (not partial). An Entra Connect sync that cannot run after the verified AD writes is not an error of the run (Pending, exit code 2, the transfer package is written).

Note

The cloud account is confirmed, never found by UPN alone. A UPN can belong to another account in the cloud (a cloud-only account with the same UPN, or an account synchronised from another object when Entra ID gave the synchronised object another UPN). Before the tool reads or changes anything in the cloud for an object, it reads the Microsoft Entra ID account with that UPN and compares its onPremisesImmutableId with the source anchor that the AD phase recorded in the batch (SourceAnchor): the base64 text of the objectGUID and, when the object has one, of ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid. The account is the right one when it carries either text (they are compared exactly: they are machine identifiers, letter case counts). In phase Both this is part of the pre-check, before any AD write.

A different account, a cloud-only account, two accounts, or an account synchronised under another UPN is an error for that object: nothing is read in Exchange Online for it and nothing is changed on it. The message says which case it is and what to do (give one of the two accounts another UPN, or remove the duplicate, then run the same command again). The Exchange Online object found by UPN must then carry the ExternalDirectoryObjectId of the confirmed account, in every read (recipient, mailbox, permissions, retention check); another object stops the call. For a shared mailbox the same check is made for each trustee of a permission to grant (the batch records their anchors, SharedTrusteeAnchors; a trustee without recorded anchors must at least be a synchronised account, not a cloud-only one), so that a permission is never granted to another person. An object that is not in Microsoft Entra ID yet is waited for like any object that is not ready.

Older batches and the records without an anchor. A batch, backup or transfer package written before 3.2.0 has no SourceAnchor: the anchor is derived from the ObjectGuid of the record (the usual source anchor), and an error then says that the record is old. A tenant whose source anchor is neither the objectGUID nor ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid (or whose ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid differs from the objectGUID in a batch of an older version) can set Cloud.IdentityCheck = 'Off' after checking the accounts by hand: accounts are then found by UPN only, and the run says so once. A Check -Identity <UPN> has no AD record at all: the account is found by UPN with a warning, and no permission is ever granted for such a record. The retention check reads an inactive mailbox (its account is deleted) by UPN only, and says so with a warning. When the account of the object is confirmed, an inactive mailbox with the same UPN that carries another ExternalDirectoryObjectId belongs to an earlier account: the check says not this object's mailbox, that mailbox never decides the verdict, and the object is reported as having no mailbox to retain (the same visible warning as an object that has no mailbox in Exchange Online; the Recover goes on, nothing is retained for it). This is not an unverified object. An inactive mailbox that carries no ExternalDirectoryObjectId at all is a candidate found by UPN (with the same warning). Several candidates are told apart by the mailbox GUID that the batch recorded from Active Directory (msExchMailboxGuid, for an object that had an on-premises mailbox); when the record has none, or it matches none or several, the check stops (nothing tells which one is the object's) and the message gives the Get-EXOMailbox -InactiveMailboxOnly command that lists them. In the deprovisioning check of a Recover only an explicit not found for the object's id counts as an absent mailbox: any other error, a 404 that does not name the id included, is a failed read, never a confirmation.

Permissions are written with the confirmed id. The Exchange Online object of a confirmed account is read with the -ExternalDirectoryObjectId parameter (recipient, mailbox, permissions), and a permission is written (Add-MailboxPermission, Add-RecipientPermission, Set-Mailbox) with the confirmed id of the mailbox and of the trustee in -Identity, -User and -Trustee. The UPN is used only for an object that has no confirmed account (Cloud.IdentityCheck = 'Off'). A grant that the run already sent (mailbox, right, trustee) is never sent again in the same run. If a later read does not show it, it is not counted as verified: the object ends done with warnings, and the warning names the permission to check by hand.

Note

Throttling and temporary failures do not end an object. A read of Microsoft Graph or Exchange Online that fails with HTTP 408, 429, 502, 503, 504, a timeout or no answer at all is sent again (at most five tries, after the Retry-After of the answer, or 5, 10, 20, 40 seconds), within Cloud.RetryBudgetObjectSeconds for one object and Cloud.RetryBudgetRunMinutes for the whole run; every retry is in the log (Detail level). A throttled answer (429, 503) also slows every following call of the run (a pause that doubles up to 30 seconds and halves after each success), so that a batch of thousands of objects does not turn into thousands of refused calls. An object whose own budget is used up stays pending and is read again at the next check of the wait; only at the end of the wait is it an error ("Microsoft 365 could not be read"). When the budget of the run is used up, the cloud part stops with one error (not one per object), the objects not finished stay Pending, and the Next steps give the command to run again a few minutes later. Any other failure (a 4xx other than 408 and 429, a refusal, a bad answer) is not sent again. A grant is never sent again: the next run finds the permission already granted or grants it.

Tip

Two servers are supported. If no single server reaches both Active Directory and Microsoft 365 (for example an AD server on an isolated network), run the AD part with -Phase AD on the AD server, copy the transfer package it writes (the .zip and its .sha256 file, both in Backups\Outbox\, chapter 10), and run -Phase Cloud -Batch <package.zip> on the cloud server. That is not a server hosted in the cloud: it is any Windows machine of the organisation that reaches Microsoft 365 through the Internet (server room or administrator workstation), with no access to AD. The summary of each step prints the command of the next one.

Part IISet up
Chapter 4

Prerequisites

In short: Install PowerShell 7.5 and three modules, then ask for the rights of the Permissions table. Nothing needs Domain Admin: the exact rights come from the code.

Server or workstation

Item AD server (phase AD / Both) Cloud server (phase Cloud / Both)
PowerShell 7.5 or later (pwsh.exe; Windows PowerShell 5.1 is refused) required required
RSAT module ActiveDirectory (loaded natively by PowerShell 7 on Windows 10 1809+ / Windows Server 2019+) required not required for phase Cloud; final AD restoration always runs separately
Entra Connect the tool runs on the Entra Connect server (module ADSync, loaded through the Windows PowerShell compatibility layer), or WinRM to EntraConnect.Server (the cycle then runs in the Windows PowerShell 5.1 endpoint of that server) —
ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.10.1 or later, installed for PowerShell 7 phase Both required
Microsoft.Graph.Authentication and Microsoft.Graph.Users 2.41.1 or later, in one same version for both, installed for PowerShell 7 phase Both required
Durable disk for Backups required required (copies of the batches)

The cloud server is not a machine hosted in the cloud: it is any Windows machine of the organisation that can reach Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph) through the Internet, in your own server room or an administrator workstation. It needs no access to Active Directory, no RSAT and no Entra Connect. It needs the rows of the Cloud server column, the same signed package folder, and a configuration file with the same Environment.

PowerShell
# PowerShell 7.5+ (pwsh), as administrator. winget install Microsoft.PowerShell installs PowerShell 7 if needed.
Install-WindowsFeature RSAT-AD-PowerShell                       # Windows Server (client: RSAT optional feature)
Install-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement -MinimumVersion 3.10.1 -Scope AllUsers -Force
Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Authentication -MinimumVersion 2.41.1 -Scope AllUsers -Force     # one command per module: PowerShellGet refuses -MinimumVersion with several names
Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Users -MinimumVersion 2.41.1 -Scope AllUsers -Force

Note

Run the tool in a new PowerShell 7 window: it refuses an Exchange Online or Microsoft Graph session that already exists in the console (it must know which session it signs out).

Window: PowerShell 7.5+ (.NET 9+) supplies the native WPF Fluent controls; there is no other window. The window launches every actual operation in a fresh PowerShell 7.5+ process (pwsh.exe of the window's own $PSHOME) on the same computer, under the same Windows account; the child inherits PSModulePath.

Installing the modules for PowerShell 7. Install-Module run in Windows PowerShell 5.1 installs under WindowsPowerShell\Modules, which PowerShell 7 does not search by default for modules without Core support. Run the Install-Module commands above from pwsh. The Windows PowerShell 5.1 copies of 2.x are not used by 3.0.0.

Permissions

Note

This list is derived from the code: every cmdlet that the engine calls was read in PRA.Directory.psm1, PRA.Cloud.psm1 and PRA.Gui.Directory.ps1, and each line names the place that justifies it (file:line of this source). What the code cannot tell is listed in What the code cannot tell you below: have it confirmed once in a lab, before the real day. A test (tests\PraDocumentation.Tests.ps1) fails if the Graph scope documented here differs from the one in the code, or if a cloud cmdlet of the code is missing from this chapter. The plain "ask your administrator" version is in the user guide.

There is nothing to give to "everybody": the account that runs the Active Directory phases and the account (or application) that runs the cloud phases can be two different identities, one per server.

Active Directory (account that runs the phases AD, Both and Finalize)

What the tool does Cmdlet Minimum right Code
Writes a user or a shared mailbox object Set-ADUser -Replace / -Clear Write property on these 10 attributes of the user objects in scope: homeMDB, homeMTA, msExchHomeServerName, msExchMailboxGuid, mDBUseDefaults, msExchRecipientDisplayType, msExchRecipientTypeDetails, msExchRemoteRecipientType, targetAddress, proxyAddresses PRA.Directory.psm1:60 (the list), :1492 (the write)
Writes the retention tag (Convert, restored by Recover/Finalize) Set-ADUser Write property on one extensionAttributeN (1 to 15; extensionAttribute1 by default). Not needed when Retention.Tag.Enabled = $false :1068-1071, :1097, :1135-1141
Puts a user in / out of the licence group (users only; never shared mailboxes) Add-ADGroupMember, Remove-ADGroupMember (-Members <user GUID>) Write property on member of the one licence group (Licensing.GroupDN). Not needed when Licensing.Enabled = $false :1500-1501
Reads the objects Get-ADUser (-Properties the 10 attributes + memberOf, uSNChanged, DisplayName, mail, mailNickname, msExchArchiveGUID, and for the backup *, msExchMailboxSecurityDescriptor, nTSecurityDescriptor, publicDelegates) Read on the user objects in scope, including Read permissions (needed to read nTSecurityDescriptor: SendAs holders) :401-410, :943-953
Reads groups and trustees Get-ADGroup, Get-ADGroupMember -Recursive, Get-ADObject -Filter objectSid / -Identity Read (default for authenticated users) :435, :481, :847, :894, :1007
Finds the domain controller, the root and the OU Get-ADDomainController, Get-ADRootDSE, Get-ADObject; Get-ADOrganizationalUnit (console OU list) Read (default for authenticated users); Active Directory Web Services (TCP 9389) reachable on the domain controller :363-378, PRA.Gui.Directory.ps1:81
Optional forced replication (Directory.ForceReplication, off by default) Sync-ADObject -Object <DN> -Source <written DC> -Destination <DC>, then Get-ADUser on each destination The control access right Replication synchronization (DS-Replication-Synchronize) on the root of the domain, for each destination domain controller. The access denied message of the tool names the same right, Replication Synchronization. The licence group is replicated too (when Licensing.Enabled) :1641, :1669, :1684, :1704

The tool never creates or deletes an AD object, never writes an ACL, never resets a password, and never writes any attribute other than those above. Domain Admins is not required by the code: only the rights of this table.

Delegate them in plain steps (a domain administrator does this once, on the OU that holds the mailboxes, to a dedicated group CONTOSO\PRA-Operators that contains the account of the operator):

  1. Create the group PRA-Operators and put the operator account in it.
  2. For the user objects: right-click the OU › Delegate Control… › the group › Create a custom task to delegate › Only the following objects in the folder › User objects › Property-specific › tick Write for the 10 attributes (and the one extensionAttribute). The same with dsacls, which is repeatable and can be reviewed:
PowerShell
# Run as a domain administrator, in PowerShell 7, once. Change the OU, the group and the attribute of the retention tag to yours.
$ou  = 'OU=Mailboxes,DC=contoso,DC=com'
$who = 'CONTOSO\PRA-Operators'
foreach ($attribute in 'homeMDB', 'homeMTA', 'msExchHomeServerName', 'msExchMailboxGuid', 'mDBUseDefaults', 'msExchRecipientDisplayType',
                       'msExchRecipientTypeDetails', 'msExchRemoteRecipientType', 'targetAddress', 'proxyAddresses', 'extensionAttribute1') {
    dsacls $ou /I:S /G "${who}:WP;$attribute;user"
}
# The licence group: add and remove members (the attribute is member).
dsacls 'CN=PRA-Licence,OU=Groups,DC=contoso,DC=com' /G "${who}:WP;member"
# Only if you turn on Directory.ForceReplication: replicate a single object (root of the domain).
dsacls 'DC=contoso,DC=com' /G "${who}:CA;Replication synchronization"
  1. Check the result: dsacls $ou lists the entries of the group; then run a Preview and an Apply on one test mailbox (user guide, Path 1) with this account.

Microsoft Graph

Interactive sign-in (a person, Windows broker) Certificate sign-in (application, nobody present)
Delegated scopes requested by the code User.Read.All (the only scope: Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.Read.All', PRA.Cloud.psm1:595) none (no scope is requested)
Application permissions none User.Read.All (Microsoft Graph, type Application)
Admin consent Yes, once: an administrator accepts User.Read.All for the organisation the first time (the sign-in window shows Permissions requested) Yes: Grant admin consent on the application registration
What it reads Get-MgUser -UserId <UPN> -Property id,userPrincipalName,onPremisesImmutableId,onPremisesSyncEnabled (the account of each object and of each trustee, once per run; and Get-MgUser -Filter "onPremisesImmutableId eq '<anchor>'" only when the UPN does not give the right account); Get-MgUser -UserId <UPN> -Property Id,UserPrincipalName (pre-check); Get-MgUser -Property assignedPlans, provisionedPlans, assignedLicenses; Get-MgUserLicenseDetail -UserId <UPN> -All the same calls
Sign-in the admin who signs in needs a role that can read other users' licences: see What the code cannot tell you Connect-MgGraph -ClientId <AppId> -CertificateThumbprint <thumbprint> -TenantId <GUID> (:595)

The tool never writes anything through Microsoft Graph. Since 3.2.0 it reads Microsoft Graph for every object (shared mailboxes and runs without a licence check included), and for every trustee of a permission to grant, to confirm the account (chapter 3): User.Read.All must be consented (delegated: the signing-in administrator; application: admin consent on the app registration) for every run of the cloud part, and the read is skipped only with Cloud.IdentityCheck = 'Off'. A refusal by Graph (403, insufficient privileges) stops the object with a message that names User.Read.All and the Off alternative; in phase Both the pre-check stops before any AD write. The account is read by its UPN once, then by its confirmed id. The licence and the provisioning are read for user mailboxes only (a shared mailbox has no licence and is checked through Exchange Online), and only when Cloud.CheckLicense is $true (the default) or Cloud.MailboxCheckVia = 'Graph'. Every Graph read is sent again after a temporary failure, within the retry budgets of the configuration.

Exchange Online

What the tool does Cmdlet Code
Finds a recipient or a mailbox, its type, its holds; the object found by UPN must carry the ExternalDirectoryObjectId of the Entra ID account confirmed for the object Get-EXORecipient, Get-EXOMailbox (also -InactiveMailboxOnly) PRA.Cloud.psm1:157, :186-187, :292
Reads the FullAccess and SendAs holders of a shared mailbox Get-EXOMailboxPermission, Get-EXORecipientPermission :252-253, :262-263
Reads the SendOnBehalf holders Get-Mailbox -Filter (property GrantSendOnBehalfTo) :283
Grants FullAccess (Convert, shared mailboxes only) Add-MailboxPermission -AccessRights FullAccess :359
Grants SendAs Add-RecipientPermission -AccessRights SendAs :360
Grants SendOnBehalf Set-Mailbox -GrantSendOnBehalfTo @{Add=...} :361
Optional (Retention.UseComplianceSession = $true, interactive only): finds the GUID of the retention policy Connect-IPPSSession, Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy :1067, :1073

There is no Remove-*, New-*, Enable-* or recovery cmdlet: a Recover never deletes a cloud mailbox by an Exchange Online call. The cloud mailbox disappears when Entra ID and Exchange Online process the AD change (the tool only waits and checks).

Interactive sign-in (a person) Certificate sign-in (application)
Role Exchange Recipient Administrator (Microsoft Entra role), or the Exchange Online role group Recipient Management. Read-only checks (Check) only: View-Only Recipients is enough The application needs the application permission Office 365 Exchange Online › Exchange.ManageAsApp (admin consent) and the Entra role Exchange Recipient Administrator assigned to its service principal (a role that Microsoft lists as supported for app-only sign-in)
Why this role it contains the Mail Recipients management role that carries Add-MailboxPermission, Set-Mailbox and the recipient reads same roles; the access token carries the directory role
Certificate none in the CurrentUser\My store of the account that runs the tool (Microsoft: -CertificateThumbprint reads the user store), with its private key, not expired (the console's Sign-in: Certificate light checks the thumbprint, the expiry and the private key), created with a CSP key provider (a CNG key is refused by Exchange Online): annex C

What the code cannot tell you (have it confirmed in a lab)

These points depend on Microsoft services or on your directory, not on the code. They are not invented here: they are the best documented answer, marked for validation.

  1. The Entra role of the person for the Graph reads. The code asks for User.Read.All (delegated). Which role the signed-in admin needs to read assignedLicenses, assignedPlans and licenseDetails of other users is decided by Microsoft Graph, not by this code. Global Reader is known to be sufficient and is the one to give; whether the Exchange Recipient Administrator role alone is enough must be tested: sign in with only that role and run Check on one user; an Authorization_RequestDenied means a reader role is missing.
  2. Which right replicates a single object. The tool says Replication Synchronization in its access denied message (PRA.Directory.psm1:1675). Microsoft's protocol document for the replicateSingleObject operation (MS-ADTS 3.1.1.3.3.18) names the same control access right, DS-Replication-Synchronize (Replication synchronization, 1131f6ab-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2), on the root of the naming context. The delegation above grants it. This has not been run with a delegated account yet. If access denied persists on a destination domain controller, add Replicating Directory Changes in the same way and report it.
  3. That an attribute-level Write property ACE is enough for every msExch* attribute with Set-ADUser from a non-Exchange account. It is how Active Directory works, but it was validated in the lab with an administrator account only (annex B).
  4. The exact Exchange role of each cmdlet. Check it in your tenant: Get-ManagementRoleEntry "*\Add-MailboxPermission","*\Add-RecipientPermission","*\Set-Mailbox","*\Get-EXOMailbox" lists the roles that carry each cmdlet; a custom role group with exactly those roles is a narrower alternative to Exchange Recipient Administrator (Microsoft, Option 2: custom role groups of the app-only authentication article).
  5. ADSyncOperators as the only membership for Get-ADSyncScheduler / Start-ADSyncSyncCycle, and Remote Management Users for the remote session: Microsoft documentation, not exercised by the tests.
  6. How Exchange Online and Entra expose the X500 addresses. The X500 control reads EmailAddresses (Get-EXOMailbox -Properties EmailAddresses) or, through Graph, proxyAddresses, and assumes that Entra Connect writes the on-premises legacyExchangeDN as an X500 address of the cloud object (the normal hybrid result). The lag (how many minutes a value takes to appear) and the property behaviour of your tenant are marked for lab validation; if the property is not returned, the control warns could not be verified instead of failing.
  7. The certificate store. The console light looks in CurrentUser\My only, the store that Exchange Online (Connect-ExchangeOnline -CertificateThumbprint) reads: a thumbprint that exists only in LocalMachine\My shows a red light. A green light still does not prove that Exchange Online accepts the certificate (CSP key, application permission): the sign-in is proven by a Check on one mailbox.

Certificate sign-in for unattended runs: annex C.

Chapter 5

Installation

In short: Copy the signed package to the server, unblock it, and put Backups on a safe disk. The package checks itself at every start.

  1. Install PowerShell 7.5 or later on the server (winget install Microsoft.PowerShell, or the MSI of the PowerShell release page), then the modules for PowerShell 7 (chapter 4). Copy the package folder (PraRemoteMailbox-3.0.0, the signed package built by tools\New-PraPackage.ps1, or the extracted release ZIP) to the server, for example D:\PRA\PraRemoteMailbox.
  2. Unblock the files if they were downloaded: Get-ChildItem D:\PRA\PraRemoteMailbox -Recurse -File -Force | Unblock-File.
  3. Put Backups on a durable volume (default: .\Backups in the tool folder; see Storage.BackupFolder).
  4. Fill in the configuration (chapter 6), then run a Preview: it checks the configuration, AD access and the scope without writing anything.

Two servers: install the same version on both, with a configuration of the same Environment (a batch is refused by a configuration of another Environment). The cloud server (any Windows machine that reaches Microsoft 365, see chapter 4) needs only the cloud sections; the AD server needs the AD sections.

Folder Content
Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 the only script to run
PraRemoteMailbox.psd1, PraRemoteMailbox.psm1 module manifest and root module: the script imports the manifest, which loads PRA.Common and PRA.Directory (PRA.Cloud and PRA.Gui are loaded only when needed)
config\ PraRemoteMailbox.config.psd1 + CSV samples
module\ PRA.Common (console, log, configuration, reports, tool version), PRA.Directory (AD), PRA.Backup (capture), PRA.Cloud (Exchange Online, Graph), PRA.Gui.psm1 and PRA.Gui.xaml (window), PRA.Gui.Directory.ps1 (read-only OU list for the window, separate process), Test-PackageIntegrity.ps1 (package verifier)
templates\ HTML report template
docs\ this guide (Markdown + HTML) and its images
PackageIntegrity.psd1 owner-signed manifest: SHA256 of every stable file
README.md, LICENSE, CHANGELOG.md project information (CHANGELOG.md is added by the package builder and is hashed by the manifest)
Backups\, logs\, reports\ created by the runs; Backups\, logs\ and reports\ are created with a private ACL (current account, SYSTEM, Administrators; no inheritance)

Package integrity

The installed package is verified every time it starts. module\Test-PackageIntegrity.ps1 and PackageIntegrity.psd1 must carry the owner's timestamped Authenticode signature (certificate thumbprint 0F28E442889F17B5F4D251E8F96E7CC6E2C9C6D6), every PowerShell file of the package must be signed by the same owner, and every stable file (modules, XAML, report template, sample CSV files, README, licence, change log, guide, images) must match the signed manifest. A changed, missing, duplicated, unexpected or reparse-point file stops Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1, the modules and the GUI helper before any import, window or operation. There is no unsigned mode, no switch and no environment variable to bypass it. Not covered, on purpose: config\PraRemoteMailbox.config.psd1 and the CSV lists you keep in config\ (your data) and the generated Backups\, logs\ and reports\. A signature detects a change; it does not stop the file system from being written.

Output folders. Storage.BackupFolder, Logging.Folder and Report.Folder must be either a folder outside the package or, inside the package, exactly the canonical Backups, logs and reports folder (a sub-folder of its own canonical folder is accepted, the name is case-sensitive). Any other folder inside the package, such as .\audit, is refused with a clear message before a file is written, because the integrity check would reject the unexpected files at the next start. Choose an external path for a custom location. The test uses the physical location resolved by Windows: a \\?\ prefix, an 8.3 name, a junction, a SUBST drive or an alias such as C:\Documents and Settings cannot hide the package (an accepted canonical folder is then used under its physical path), and a path whose location cannot be resolved is refused rather than assumed to be external.

Chapter 6

Configuration

In short: One settings file says who is converted and which groups and servers are used. Change only the lines you need: a wrong or unknown line is refused.

Everything is set in config\PraRemoteMailbox.config.psd1 — the command line only chooses the action. The file is a PowerShell data file: text between quotes, $true / $false, numbers, @( ) for lists. An unknown setting is refused (a typing mistake never goes unnoticed). Relative paths are relative to the tool folder.

Identity of the environment

Setting Meaning
Environment Label used in the backup file names; a batch is only accepted by a configuration of the same Environment.
DomainController The writable DC used for every read and write of a run. Keep it fixed: AD versions (uSNChanged) are per DC, and the final restore of a Recover must use the DC of the AD phase.

Scope — which mailboxes are converted

Setting Meaning
Scope.Mode Only a new conversion (Convert, phase AD or Both, without -Identity or -Batch) needs it: Check, the cloud phases, Recover and Finalize never read the scope, so a server without it (the cloud server) works. If it is empty (for instance OU without SearchBase, the default file) a conversion stops with Scope.Mode = OU requires Scope.SearchBase: no OU is set ... Fill it in the configuration file, or give -Identity, -CsvPath, -SearchBase or -Group for this run, or set Scope.Mode = Auto. Values: OU (every on-premises mailbox under SearchBase), Auto (same, SearchBase optional = whole domain), Group (members of GroupDN, recursive), Csv (column Identity in CsvPath).
Scope.IncludeShared, IncludeRoom, IncludeEquip Mailbox types included besides user mailboxes.
Scope.ExcludeSamAccountNames Accounts never converted. System mailboxes are always excluded.

-Identity converts one object instead of the scope, whatever its type: -Scope is ignored with -Identity on Convert (a user, a shared mailbox, a room or an equipment mailbox that the eligibility rules accept). -Scope UsersOnly|SharedOnly and -MaxObjects N narrow a run on the configured scope (a pilot, a first wave); -Scope still filters a batch for Recover, the cloud phase and Check.

Conversion

Setting Meaning
Remote.RecipientType msExchRemoteRecipientType of users: 1 (provision a mailbox) or 3 (provision a mailbox and its archive); any other value is refused. With 1, +2 is added automatically when the user has an on-premises archive and HandleArchives = $true.
Remote.HandleArchives $true (default): add the archive bit (2) for a user who has an on-premises archive.
Remote.ClearMailboxGuid $true: clear msExchMailboxGuid, a new empty cloud mailbox is created.
Routing.RoutingDomain tenant.mail.onmicrosoft.com — domain of the targetAddress. AutoDetect reuses an existing proxy address in this domain.
Licensing.Enabled $true (default): users are added to the licence group at Convert and removed again at Recover (unless they were members before). $false: the licence is handled outside the tool.
Licensing.GroupDN AD group, synchronised to Entra ID, that carries the Exchange Online licence (group-based licensing). Required when Licensing.Enabled = $true.

Shared mailboxes

Setting Meaning
SharedMailbox.Enabled $true (default): shared mailboxes are converted with their permissions (when Scope.IncludeShared = $true). $false: no permission is captured or granted.
SharedMailbox.RemoteRecipientType 97 (first provisioning of a shared mailbox), 99 with archive.
SharedMailbox.PermissionSource Where FullAccess / SendAs holders are read, without Exchange: AD (default: the copy Exchange keeps on the account), Csv (Shared,Group), CustomAttribute (a group tagged with the name of the mailbox), None. Groups are expanded to their users. Details: chapter 2, Shared mailbox permissions.
CaptureSendOnBehalf SendOnBehalf holders from publicDelegates.
GrantFullAccess, GrantSendAs, GrantSendOnBehalf, AutoMapping What is granted in Exchange Online. The values of Enabled, PermissionSource and the three Grant... settings in force at the Convert are stored in the batch (GrantSettings); the cloud phase of any server follows the batch. When the configuration of the cloud server differs, a warning names the values used (the batch's). A batch written before 3.2.0 has none: the configuration of the server is used, with a warning. A permission that the batch carries and the settings in force do not grant (old batch, or a batch converted with settings that grant none) is never silent: the run ends done with warnings, the warning names each permission (FullAccess, SendAs, SendOnBehalf and the trustee), and the report and the CSV say to grant by hand (the lists are also in the backup file).
ExcludeTrusteeSamAccountNames Accounts never reproduced (e.g. service or admin accounts found in the ACLs).
KeepCloudSharedOnRecover $true = Recover keeps the cloud shared mailbox (rare).
DeferOnPremRestore With phase Both, $true defers final AD restoration to Finalize. Phase Cloud always packages it, regardless of this setting.

Entra Connect

Setting Meaning
EntraConnect.Sync $true: after the AD writes, run one cycle and wait for its end. Checked before the first AD write, with the account that runs the tool: an authenticated, read-only call to the ADSync module of the server (Test-WSMan is not used: it does not authenticate). If the check fails, Apply stops with "Entra Connect sync will not be possible: ..." (the reason and what to do), before the confirmation, with no backup and no write; Preview reports the same text as a warning. $false: the operator synchronises.
EntraConnect.Server Entra Connect server reached by PowerShell remoting (bounded time); empty = this server (ADSync module). The console tries it too, in the background, and shows the answer on the Entra Connect light of the Setup page.
EntraConnect.PolicyType, TimeoutMinutes Delta (default) or Initial; how long to wait for the cycle.

Active Directory replication (optional)

The attributes are written on ONE domain controller. Entra Connect reads the domain controller it is attached to: if the change has not replicated there yet, the delta synchronisation runs for nothing. When the replication delay of the domain is a problem, turn this option on; it is off by default.

Setting Meaning
Directory.ForceReplication $true: a step Active Directory replication runs just before the Entra Connect step (Convert AD or Both, Recover AD or Both, Finalize). For each object changed in the run it calls Sync-ADObject -Object <DN> -Source <written DC> -Destination <DC> towards every other writable domain controller, then reads the changed attributes back on each of them and compares them with the expected state. Also -ForceAdReplication (one run) and the checkbox Replicate Active Directory before the Entra Connect sync in the run settings of the console (marked modified, part of the effective configuration and of the Preview guard).
Directory.ReplicationTargets Optional list of domain controllers to restrict it to (for example the ones the Entra Connect connector reads). Empty = every other writable domain controller of the domain.
Directory.ReplicationVerifyAttempts, ReplicationVerifyDelaySeconds Bounded read-back: 1..30 reads, 1..60 seconds apart (6 and 10 by default). One progress event per attempt, one item event per object and domain controller.

A Preview never replicates (the step is only listed, as skipped, when the option is on). Nothing is silent: a domain controller that is unreachable, not approved or that does not converge is a warning that names it; the synchronisation still runs, and the Next steps say that it may not have seen the change and how to run it again later (Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta on the Entra Connect server). Rights: replicating a single object needs the right Replication Synchronization (the extended right DS-Replication-Synchronize) on the domain naming context (normally Domain Admins); an access denied is reported with that sentence. The licence group (when Licensing.Enabled) is replicated and read back like the users. With an explicit -Confirm, PowerShell asks once per destination domain controller.

Microsoft 365

Setting Meaning
Cloud.TenantId, Cloud.Organization Tenant GUID and initial domain (tenant.onmicrosoft.com). Every session is checked against them. When Cloud.AppId is set, both are required (the tenant must be a GUID): the configuration is refused at load otherwise.
Cloud.AppId + Cloud.CertificateThumbprint Certificate sign-in (unattended, annex C). Both empty = interactive sign-in (Cloud.UserPrincipalName = expected account).
Cloud.CheckMailbox, CheckLicense, MailboxCheckVia, RequiredSkuPartNumber What "ready" means for a user: mailbox (Exchange Online type, or Graph provisioning) and licence. MailboxCheckVia is Exo by default (mailbox type in Exchange Online) or Graph (provisioning).
Cloud.IdentityCheck Anchor (default): the Entra ID account of every object, and of every trustee of a permission to grant, must carry the Active Directory source anchor (onPremisesImmutableId = base64 of the objectGUID or of ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid): another account, a cloud-only account or an ambiguous answer is an error for the object and nothing is changed on it (chapter 3). Off: accounts are found by UPN only, with one notice per run; for a tenant whose source anchor is another attribute. Any letter case.
Cloud.RetryBudgetObjectSeconds, Cloud.RetryBudgetRunMinutes How long a read of Microsoft Graph or Exchange Online that fails with 408, 429, 502, 503, 504, a timeout or no answer may wait in retries: at most RetryBudgetObjectSeconds seconds for one object (default 180, 0 to 3600) and RetryBudgetRunMinutes minutes for the whole run (default 30, 0 to 720). 0 = no retry. A run that used up its budget stops with one error and the command to run again; an object that used up its own stays pending until the wait ends.
Exo.MinModuleVersion Oldest ExchangeOnlineManagement accepted (default 3.10.1, which is also the lowest value used: a lower setting is raised to it). With an older module the tool stops before any change and gives the Install-Module command; Exo.UseSubprocess is the only way to the child process. The Microsoft Graph minimum (2.41.1, one same version for Authentication and Users) is fixed in the tool.
Exo.DisableWAM $false (default): interactive sign-in through the Windows broker (WAM). $true: browser sign-in instead. See chapter 8, Cloud sign-in from the window.
Exo.GrantVerifyAttempts, GrantVerifyDelaySeconds After one grant, re-read up to N times (never granted twice).
Exo.UseSubprocess Run every Exchange Online call in a child PowerShell 7 process (certificate only; automatic with a module older than MinModuleVersion).
Polling.IntervalMinutes, TimeoutMinutes How often (default 1 minute) and how long (default 60) the cloud part waits (15 to 60 minutes is common after a sync).

Retention

Setting Meaning
Retention.Enabled $true (default): the retention tag is written at Convert and restored at Recover.
Retention.PolicyName, PolicyGuid The Purview retention policy used by -Action Check -Expect Retained and by the retention check before a Recover (default name PRA-Converted-Retention; the policy is created outside the tool). PolicyGuid is used directly when set.
Retention.UseComplianceSession $true: find the GUID from PolicyName through an interactive Connect-IPPSSession.
Retention.ProofMaxAgeHours 24 (default), 1 to 720: how old a retention proof from the cloud server may be to stand in for the check on the AD server (see Two servers below).
Retention.CheckBeforeRecover $true (default): before it removes the cloud mailboxes, a Recover reads each mailbox that carries the retention tag and checks that the retention policy holds it (see below). $false: no check, in every run; each Recover says so once, in a warning, and never claims that the check passed.
Retention.Tag.Enabled, Attribute, Value The AD attribute (extensionAttribute1 to 15) and the value (Converted) written at Convert.

Retention.Tag writes Converted in extensionAttribute1 (by default) at Convert. In Exchange Online it becomes CustomAttribute1: an adaptive scope of a Purview retention policy can use it, so that the cloud mailbox is kept (inactive mailbox) when Recover deprovisions it. The policy itself is created outside the tool; -Action Check -Expect Retained checks the holds (PolicyGuid).

The retention check before a Recover (Retention.CheckBeforeRecover, on by default). A Recover removes the cloud mailboxes, so before the confirmation, in the Preview and in the Apply (phase Both or AD), it reads in Exchange Online each mailbox whose record carries the retention tag and checks that the policy of Retention.PolicyGuid holds it. From 20 objects, the active mailboxes that carry the tag are read in bulk: one server-side search for about 50 objects ((CustomAttribute<N> -eq '<value>') -and ((UserPrincipalName -eq '<upn>') -or ...), so 100 searches for 5,000 objects instead of 5,000 reads), and each object is matched in memory by the Entra ID account confirmed for it, else by its UPN, when exactly one tagged active mailbox answers. Every other object (no tagged active mailbox, several, an inactive mailbox, an ambiguity) is read on its own, and the rules of that read decide: the two ways always give the same answer. No bulk read is made once a failure has stopped the reads. Microsoft Entra ID accounts are still confirmed one by one, and kept for the cloud part of a run in phase Both. The check has its own retry budget (Cloud.RetryBudgetObjectSeconds, Cloud.RetryBudgetRunMinutes): what it spends is not taken from the cloud part that follows. A mailbox with no cloud mailbox has nothing to retain: the run does not stop for it, but it says so with a warning for each such object (the first ten, all in the log) and one warning with their count, because a mailbox is expected after a Convert whose cloud part completed (the warning is only logged for an object whose cloud part is recorded as not completed). A mailbox kept on purpose (SharedMailbox.KeepCloudSharedOnRecover) is not read.

Answer Preview Apply
Every mailbox is held one line says so goes on
A mailbox is not held (not in the policy, excluded, delete-only, an adaptive scope that has not caught up), or cannot be checked (Retention.PolicyGuid empty, Microsoft 365 not reachable from this server, the cloud modules missing) warnings name the first ten mailboxes (all are in the log) and say that the Apply will be refused stops before any change, exit code 1: the reason, then the commands to go on (the read-only Check -Expect Retained for each mailbox, the Preview again, the same Apply with -AcceptRetentionRisk, and the GUID lookup when PolicyGuid is empty)
-AcceptRetentionRisk is given the Preview tells what it would accept goes on; a warning names what is accepted (console, log, summary, report), and the run lists it among the run settings changed

-AcceptRetentionRisk applies to one run and is never remembered; in the console it is a checkbox of the Recover page that stays ticked for Previews and is cleared once an Apply has run. It is accepted for the AD part of a Recover only; anywhere else the run says that it is ignored. The Next steps never carry it into a command to run again: it appears only in the line that says "to go on anyway". Retention.CheckBeforeRecover = $false turns the check off for every run: each Recover then prints one warning (The retention check before a Recover is turned off) and the settings of the report show it.

Two servers: the retention proof. The AD server often cannot reach Microsoft 365, so its Recover cannot read the retention. The cloud server reads it for it. The order is fixed: where the run can ask Exchange Online (phase Both, a certificate sign-in, or phase AD at an interactive console without -Force), Exchange Online decides and the proof is not read. Only when Exchange Online cannot be reached or asked on the AD part (a sign-in that fails for any reason: a refused or cancelled prompt, an error of the identity provider, a missing or invalid Cloud.TenantId, a missing certificate, a session that is already open; no answer; throttling or retry time used up; the cloud modules missing; the policy not named; or a run that cannot be interactive: -Force, a non-interactive host, the console) does the proof stand in, and only when every object that is not covered is unverified for that one reason. An answer about one object (a mailbox that is not held, another account, a mailbox that is not unique, an ambiguity between inactive mailboxes) blocks, and the proof is not read. Every object that carries the retention tag is checked, also one whose Exchange Online part of the Convert is not recorded as complete: the licence group that the Convert adds gives it a mailbox as soon as Entra Connect has synchronised, with or without that part, and the Recover removes the licence again; the run says so in one Info line, and an object that has no mailbox in Exchange Online passes as "no mailbox, nothing to retain". The warnings name the mailboxes concerned (the first ten, then how many more; the whole list is in the log). When a proof was read, the counts follow its verdicts: held, not held, unverified, not checked and not in the proof are counted apart. A scheduled run has no person to sign in: start it with -NonInteractive or -Force (or give it a certificate sign-in), so that it goes to the proof or to Exchange Online without a prompt. A run that cannot be interactive never starts an interactive sign-in: it goes straight to the proof. A mailbox that Exchange Online says is not held is never overruled by a proof.

  1. On the cloud server (it needs the batch folder, as for any Check): .\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Check -Batch <convert or recover batch> -Expect Retained. The Check is read only, and it also writes the retention proof in Backups\Outbox of the backup folder (also when it was started from a transfer package with -Batch <zip>, which it reads in a temporary preview folder: the run prints the real path of the proof). Each failing line names its object, an object that has no mailbox in Exchange Online passes (it is shown as no mailbox ... nothing to retain and is not counted as an error), and the Next steps of a Check that finds mailboxes not held are about the retention policy (the command that reads it, then the Check again), not about the Entra Connect sync: RetentionProof-<batch id>-<time>.json and its .sha256 file. The file holds the batch ID, the hash of the Convert batch file, the Environment, the time (UTC), the GUID of the policy that was checked and, for each object (ObjectGuid and UPN), its Verdict and the booleans Covered and NoMailbox, which always agree with it. Covered and NoMailbox (a mailbox that does not exist in Exchange Online has nothing to retain) are the two passing verdicts. NotCovered says that the policy does not hold the mailbox. Unverified says that this mailbox itself could not be checked (not unique, ambiguous between inactive mailboxes, an Entra ID account that is not the synchronised one, policy unknown, any error on that mailbox, a read that got no answer while the Check went on with the next mailbox). An inactive mailbox that belongs to an earlier account is not this object's mailbox: the object has no mailbox to retain, so its verdict is NoMailbox, not Unverified. NotChecked says that the Check stopped before it (retry time used up, Microsoft Graph refused, no network, throttling). NotCovered, Unverified and NotChecked all block. A proof without Verdict is not accepted: run the Check again.
  2. Copy the two files, together, to Backups\Inbox of the AD server (the folder where it already looks for transfer packages).
  3. On the AD server, when Exchange Online cannot be asked (see above), the Recover (-Phase AD) accepts the proof when all of these hold: its checksum matches its .sha256 file; the file is at most 64 MB and is read once (the hash and the content are the same bytes); every entry has an ObjectGuid that is a GUID (or none) and a Covered and a NoMailbox that are true or false, and no object or UPN is listed twice; its batch ID is the one of the Convert batch being rolled back and its SourceBackupHash is the hash of that batch file; its Environment is the one of the configuration; its policy is Retention.PolicyGuid when the configuration sets one (a Retention.PolicyGuid that is not a GUID refuses every proof, and the Next steps say to correct it); when this server has no Retention.PolicyGuid, the proof is accepted and the policy GUID that the proof names is printed in the OK line and in the report, so that you can compare it with the policy you expect (the Next steps give Connect-IPPSSession; Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy | Format-Table Name,Guid when Retention.PolicyName is empty too); it is not older than Retention.ProofMaxAgeHours (default 24, from 1 to 720, the setting of the server that reads the proof) and not dated in the future (more than 5 minutes ahead: the clocks of the two servers differ; compare them with Get-Date on both, or w32tm /stripchart /computer:<other server> /samples:3 /dataonly); and it says Covered (or NoMailbox) for every object of the Recover. An object is found by its ObjectGuid; its UPN is used only for a proof entry that has no ObjectGuid, so the same UPN with another ObjectGuid is not covered. Letter case does not matter for the Environment or the UPNs. The newest proof decides. The newest proof of the batch is chosen by the time in its file name (ties by name); the copies of one proof (the same SHA-256, in Inbox and in the batch folder) count once; a proof whose name time differs from the time inside it, or whose name carries a time that does not exist (a renamed file), is refused (and still counts as the newest, so it blocks). The same name in two folders with different content is settled the same way every time: the copy that is valid and named after its content first, then the full path; the reason always gives the full path, and the Next steps say which damaged copy to delete. If the newest proof cannot be used (still being copied, damaged, without its .sha256 file, dated in the future, too old, of another batch, Environment, batch file or policy), nothing is accepted and the Next steps say what to do (copy both files again and delete the damaged copy, compare the clocks, run the Check again, or, for another policy, put the same Retention.PolicyGuid on the two servers and run the full Check again, with the command that reads the GUID): an older proof never stands in for it. An incomplete newest proof is never completed by an older one: if it does not say Covered or NoMailbox for every object of the Recover, the run blocks, names the objects and the proof, and the step is to run the full Check again on the cloud server. The run then says Retention: accepted from the retention proof …, asks nothing more of Exchange Online, and records the accepted proof (file, SHA-256, creation time, policy GUID and number of objects) in the log, in the settings of the phase data and in the report (Retention proof accepted). An object that the proof says has no mailbox gets the same warning as a live answer. In any other case the Recover blocks as above, says why no proof was accepted, and the Next steps give the Check to run on the cloud server (the command is written for that server, without -ConfigPath), the folder where to bring the proof back, the Preview to run again and, last, the line that goes on anyway with -AcceptRetentionRisk. A Next step never tells you to bring a proof that the run would ignore: when Exchange Online answered, the steps are about the policy only.

The .sha256 file is an integrity check, not a proof of origin. Anyone who can write both files into Backups\Inbox (or Outbox) can make a proof that this server accepts. The control is the access to those folders: give write access to them only to the operators of the tool (the tool creates its private folders with that ACL; keep it, as for the PhaseData-* files). The proof does not replace the live check where Exchange Online can be asked: with phase Both, with a certificate sign-in, or at an interactive console, Exchange Online decides. The console shows, on the Recover task (AD part), for the objects that the Recover would check, whether a proof is found for the selected batch and how old it is, and whether this server needs it (it cannot sign in without a person) or reads it only when Exchange Online cannot be reached (certificate sign-in); the checkbox stays the override. The console's own Check tile checks one mailbox and writes no proof: use the command above.

Files

Setting Meaning
Storage.BackupFolder Backups (one private folder per batch). Durable, protected, copied outside the server.
Storage.ForbiddenBackupRoots Volumes where a backup is refused (temporary disks).
Logging.Folder, Report.Folder, Report.Enabled One log + one transcript per run; CSV + HTML report per run. Inside the package only .\logs and .\reports are accepted; use an external path for another location.
Execution.Phase Default of -Phase: Both on one server; AD or Cloud on the servers of a two-server setup.
Chapter 7

Unattended execution

In short: For a run with nobody present, the tool signs in with an application and a certificate, from a scheduled task.

For a run without a person at the keyboard (scheduled task, orchestrator):

  1. Start PowerShell 7, never powershell.exe: the action of the scheduled task is "C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe" -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File "D:\PRA\PraRemoteMailbox\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1" -Action Convert -Mode Apply -Force (adapt the path of pwsh.exe).

  2. Certificate sign-in: create the application once (annex C) and set Cloud.AppId + Cloud.CertificateThumbprint. The certificate must be in the CurrentUser\My store of the account that runs the tool.

  3. Run with -Mode Apply -Force under a domain account that has the AD rights of chapter 4. -Confirm:$false is accepted as an equivalent for the single confirmation (an explicit -Confirm, with either value, skips it); use it only after a reviewed Preview.

  4. Read the exit code: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 done but a next step is required (Pending objects). With -PassThru, the tool also returns the result object: Status, ExitCode, BatchId, NextSteps, the counters and the paths of the log and the reports (without -PassThru, nothing is written to the pipeline).

PowerShell
$r = & 'D:\PRA\PraRemoteMailbox\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1' -Action Convert -Mode Apply -Force -PassThru
if ($r.ExitCode -eq 1) { throw "PRA Convert failed: $($r.Issues[0].Message)" }
$r.BatchId      # keep it: Recover -Batch <id>
Part IIIUse
Chapter 8

Everyday use

In short: Use the console window, or copy a recipe. The routine never changes: preview, read, apply, keep the batch ID.

Everything else comes from the configuration file; the command line only says what to do this time.

Parameter Values Use
-Action Convert, Recover, Finalize, Check required for command-line operations; mutually exclusive with -Gui. The value is case-insensitive for -Action, -Mode, -Phase, -Scope and -Expect (convert, CLOUD, apply): the script rewrites them to their official spelling before anything else, and the strict comparisons of the proofs and batches stay case-sensitive
-Mode Preview (default), Apply Apply writes, after one confirmation
-Phase Both, AD, Cloud Convert / Recover on two servers; default Execution.Phase
-Batch batch ID (8 characters), path of the batch JSON, or a transfer package .zip (path, or the name of a file in Backups\Inbox, Backups\Outbox or the current folder) Recover, -Phase Cloud, Finalize; optional for Check. Also accepted by Convert -Phase AD to finish a batch left without its synchronisation or package (no AD write, see Exit codes). A package is verified, then extracted (chapter 10)
-Identity UPN, sAMAccountName, DN or GUID one object only
-SearchBase OU distinguished name Convert AD/Both only; run-specific OU + child OUs, without changing configuration
-CsvPath path of an Identity CSV Convert AD/Both only; run-specific comma/semicolon list, without changing configuration
-Group name (sAMAccountName or CN) or distinguished name of an AD group Convert AD/Both only; run-specific: the members of the group, nested groups included, without changing configuration. Computers, contacts and users without an on-premises mailbox are listed as skipped, with the reason. Not with -Identity, -SearchBase or -CsvPath. A name that matches no group, or two groups, is refused
-Scope All (default), UsersOnly, SharedOnly filters the scope or the batch; ignored by Convert with -Identity
-MaxObjects number (0 = no limit) Convert: first N objects
-Expect Provisioned (default), Deprovisioned, Retained Check only
-ConfigPath path another configuration file (another environment)
-BaseConfigPath path set by the console when run settings were changed: -ConfigPath is then the effective copy and this is the file it was made from. The log, the result and the report list the settings that differ. Not needed on the command line
-Force switch Apply without the confirmation (unattended). An explicit -Confirm (with either value) also skips the single confirmation: -Confirm:$false behaves like -Force, a plain -Confirm replaces it with a PowerShell prompt for every write. Never skips a safety check.
-Once switch cloud checks: one pass, no wait
-PassThru switch also returns the result object (chapter 7)
-Gui switch opens the window; may be combined with -ConfigPath, not with an operation
-WhatIf / -Verbose switches -WhatIf = Preview; -Verbose shows the debug lines of the log

The routine is always the same: run the command without -Mode Apply (preview: nothing is written), read the plan, run the same command with -Mode Apply, answer Y, and note the batch ID printed at the end — it is the key of the roll-back. The recipes below are complete: copy them, change the names.

The console (WPF window)

PowerShell
# Native Fluent controls; the business engine runs in a separate pwsh.exe process.
pwsh -STA -File .\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Gui -ConfigPath .\config\PraRemoteMailbox.config.psd1

The console is a guided path of five pages, made for an operator under pressure: Setup, Task, Verify, Run, Next steps. Opening it, reloading the configuration or picking a batch never connects to Active Directory or Microsoft 365; the engine does that, in its own PowerShell 7.5+ process, when you click Preview or Run. The language of the console is English.

Page What it shows What it asks
1.
