Setup the environment, what this server can run (AD, Cloud or both) and the prerequisite lights: RSAT ActiveDirectory, Cloud modules (one light for ExchangeOnlineManagement, 3.10.1 or later (Exo.MinModuleVersion), and Microsoft.Graph, Authentication and Users in one same version, 2.41.1 or later; green reads Exchange Online 3.10.1, Microsoft Graph 2.41.1 (Authentication and Users); the red text says what is missing and gives the exact Install-Module commands), the Entra Connect synchronisation, and the sign-in (the certificate is looked up in CurrentUser\My (the store the sign-in reads; a thumbprint only in LocalMachine\My is red) with its expiry, or the Windows account broker). A fifth light, Microsoft 365 reachable, appears once the programs and the sign-in are in place: an HTTPS request (HEAD, port 443, through the default system proxy, 3 s) to login.microsoftonline.com and to outlook.office365.com, sent in the background (the window never waits; Choose a task stays grey for those few seconds). Any HTTP answer counts as reachable. The lights come from real detection (Get-Module -ListAvailable, the certificate stores, the network test); Check again runs it again nothing when the lights are green: read three lines, click Choose a task. One compact line, This run: PROD · dc02.contoso.com · All mailboxes · Certificate sign-in, with Change... to open the run settings
2. Task four tiles: Move mailboxes to Exchange Online, Roll back a conversion, Complete a rollback (only when a Finalize package exists) and Check a mailbox; then On what? the object source of a new Convert (below), or the batch or transfer package to continue. The phase is inferred and explained: What will happen on this server
3. Verify the plan in order, the settings used, then the result of the Preview in plain words (12 mailboxes will be converted, 2 shared, 0 blocking) and the grid of objects with what was found Preview first; the confirmation word (any letter case) unlocks Run after an identical Preview. Check has no preview and no confirmation: it never writes
4. Run the steps announced by the engine (the plan event) with a glyph per state, a counter, a bar per step and the elapsed time; explicit waits (Entra Connect synchronisation, grant verification, deprovisioning and mailbox polling: attempt 4 / 13, next check in 7 s); a status pill and an overall bar nothing: while a wait runs, the detail pane says what is awaited, the attempt, the next check and how long it may take; click a step to read what it does, its objects, its warnings and errors in plain words and, collapsed, the technical message; click an object for its journey
5. Next steps the transfer package to carry to the next server (below), the exact command, the result, the report and log, and the status of the batch (AD, Cloud, Finalize) Start a new task

Run settings (page 1, Change...): Environment, domain controller, mailbox scope (All, users only, shared only), sign-in (certificate or interactive Windows broker), tenant ID and organization. The cloud fields appear only when the chosen task needs the cloud. A value that differs from the configuration file is marked modified, with Reset. What you change applies to this run only and is never written to the file. The window writes an effective configuration (the file, plus your changes) in a private run folder (logs\gui\run-<id>\effective.config.psd1, same private ACL as the other folders), the engine loads it with the same validation as any configuration (Import-PraConfiguration), and its SHA-256 is part of the Preview guard: changing it, or the file it comes from, voids the Preview. The log and the result list the settings changed against the file (-BaseConfigPath, see the table of this chapter). The Environment is a text field (suggestions: the environments seen in the batches of the backup folder). When you pick a batch or a package, the Environment is locked to the one of the batch: a batch only continues in the environment where it started.

The object source of a new Convert is chosen on the Task page, never on Setup:

Source Selection
Single identity (test) (default) one UPN, sAMAccountName, DN or GUID: the safest way to try a run
Configured scope the Scope of the configuration file, shown read only
OU its distinguished name, or Pick an OU... to browse the OUs of the configured DC (read in a separate PowerShell 7 process, when clicked); child OUs are included
AD group the name (sAMAccountName or CN) or the distinguished name of a group; Check reads the group (read only) and shows its name and its number of members, nested groups included
CSV a list with an Identity column (UPN, sAMAccountName, DN or GUID); comma and semicolon are supported

The source is passed to the engine as -Identity, -SearchBase, -Group or -CsvPath; the configuration is not rewritten. Changing the source, the list or the CSV contents voids the previous Preview. The list is revalidated and hashed before Run. AD still verifies the real object types and complete backups before writing. Users and shared mailboxes are supported: use All (with Scope.IncludeShared = $true, the default), users only or shared only.

Task New or continue Phase (inferred) Needs
Move mailboxes new batch Both if this server can do AD and cloud and Execution.Phase is Both, otherwise AD the object source
Move mailboxes continue Cloud the Convert batch or package of the AD part
Roll back new like new batch the original Convert batch
Roll back continue Cloud the Recover batch or package (not the Convert one)
Complete a rollback AD only the Finalize package
Check a mailbox Cloud, read only one UPN

Continue a batch lists the batches found in Storage.BackupFolder (of every environment) and the transfer packages waiting in <Storage.BackupFolder>\Inbox, with their state. Import package... takes a .zip from anywhere: the console verifies it (all checks before any write, chapter 10), extracts it into Storage.BackupFolder and selects its batch. A package picked in the list is imported when you continue to the verification page.

A Convert batch whose proof is partial (it stopped at its first error: some objects were verified, the others were not converted) is labelled Partial: k of n converted, and Continue a batch offers it as finish it here (the synchronisation first, then the package, as the command line does): so is any batch whose journal has no Entra Connect entry that ended well when EntraConnect.Sync is on; the files of the global report (PhaseData-..., PhaseEvents-...) are not batches and are never listed. A Convert batch whose AD part is verified (it has its State-<id>.json) but whose Entra Connect sync did not end (the last ADSync line of its journal is Failed), or that has no package in Backups\Outbox on a server that cannot do the cloud part, is marked finish it here (orange). Selecting it makes the phase AD and runs Convert -Phase AD -Batch <path> (Exit codes): the Entra Connect check, the synchronisation again, the package; Active Directory is not written and the cloud sign-in is not needed. The Next steps page of a run whose sync could not start puts the sync before the copy of the package. An engine refusal "already converted by batch ..." sent from the console names this path (Task, Continue a batch) instead of a command line.

Sections of the list. Each row says what the batch needs, with an icon in its status pill. Rows that need attention come first, in orange: Partial: k of n converted, Cloud part pending: n objects not ready, run it again (the last cloud run left objects not ready), Cloud part stopped: run it again (it failed or was cancelled) and the finish it here rows. The other batches that are still to do follow, in the accent colour (AD part done, cloud part to do, AD rollback done, cloud part to do, Ready to finalize). The Finished rows (green check) come last, are greyed and cannot be picked in Continue a batch, Continue a rollback or Complete a rollback: Finished: cloud part done, Cloud part done: finalize on the AD server, Finalized: the directory is restored. In Roll back a conversion a finished conversion is still a batch to roll back, and says Finished · can be rolled back. Above the list, To do (n), Finished (n) and All (n) choose the section: the lists that continue a batch or finalize a rollback start on To do, the others on All, changing the mode puts the section back, and a section with nothing in it says why (for example Nothing is left to do here: 3 finished and hidden). The console reads this from the PhaseData-*.json files of the batch folder, which the cloud phase of a Convert (in the Convert batch folder), the cloud phase of a Recover (in the batch of the AD rollback) and the Finalize now leave there: the last cloud-side run of the batch decides (a later failed run reopens a finished batch), only the first 64 KB of each file are read, and the answer is kept while the file does not change. A batch with no such file (a batch of an earlier version, a folder copied by hand) is shown as still to do. A partial batch is never shown as finished, whatever its cloud part did. The letter case of the values in the file does not matter.

Safety is unchanged. Run is locked until a successful Preview of exactly the same request, files and configuration; the engine independently rereads the directory, backs up and verifies the targets before every write. Type CONVERT, RECOVER or FINALIZE (any letter case, surrounding spaces ignored). An errored, unfinished or empty preview does not unlock Run. The engine is never stopped by force and the window refuses to close while it runs. Expert mode (collapsed at the bottom of Setup) holds what a normal run does not need: a manual phase, MaxObjects, Expect, Once, another configuration file, and the equivalent command line.

Pending is not failure and not completion (exit code 2): do the next step the page tells you. The Next steps page of a failed run says what stopped, in plain words, and what to do.

Cloud sign-in from the window (WAM) and the child console

Each operation runs in its own PowerShell 7.5+ child process, started by the window. The child is the same engine as the command line; the window only reads its event file, its output and its exit code. Two choices matter for the interactive Microsoft 365 sign-in (Connect-ExchangeOnline, Connect-MgGraph):

  • The Windows account broker (WAM) is on by default (Exo.DisableWAM = $false; Microsoft Graph keeps its own default, which is also WAM). The broker needs a parent window handle. A child started with no console window (the former CreateNoWindow) has none, and the sign-in failed with an MSAL error and no window. Actions that can reach the cloud (Convert and Recover with phase Both or Cloud, and Check) are therefore started with a new console window of their own and without -NonInteractive. The window starts the child with CreateProcess and the CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE flag (bound in memory with the same Reflection.Emit technique as the physical-path check of PRA.Common: no compiler, no temporary DLL), while its three standard streams stay redirected to pipes. The child therefore does not share the console of the terminal that started the window: closing or hiding that terminal in the middle of an Apply cannot stop the engine, and the broker gets the window of the new console as its parent. The new console is titled PRA Remote Mailbox - cloud sign-in; it stays empty, because the engine's output goes to the window, not to that console. Under Windows Terminal set as the default terminal application, the new console opens as a window of Windows Terminal.
  • The child's standard input is closed at once, so a prompt receives an empty answer (end of file) instead of waiting for a keyboard, and the engine's own checks then refuse; this replaces -NonInteractive, which would also forbid the sign-in. AD-only children (phase AD, Finalize, the OU list) never sign in to the cloud and have no console window at all.

What to do: leave the new console window open (it can be minimised) while a cloud operation runs and accept the Microsoft sign-in dialog. If the sign-in dialog cannot open, use the certificate sign-in (annex C) or set Exo.DisableWAM = $true (browser sign-in). The activity log shows the engine's own console lines as they arrive (sign-in messages, waits, warnings), without repeating the events it already displays; the complete output is kept in logs\gui\<id>.stdout.txt and .stderr.txt (the raw bytes of the child, in the console code page of the computer). The activity log keeps the last 2,000 lines of a run: its header says where the complete log is (the file of the engine once the run has ended).

What the window leaves behind. When it opens, the window removes what it left in logs\gui more than 30 days ago (the event and output files of the runs, the results of the lookups, and the run-... folders with the effective copy of the configuration of a run); the logs and the reports of the engine are not in that folder and stay. Ctrl+C typed in the console that started the window is not sent to the window (it would stop the window and its handlers): close the window, or wait for a run to end. The OU lookup (Pick an OU...) stops after 60 seconds with a message when the domain controller does not answer, and the window can be closed again. After a valid run, a step that was announced and not run is shown as skipped, not as waiting.

Recover and the retention check. On the Recover task, when the AD part runs on this server, the Task page shows a checkbox, Go on even if the retention policy does not hold every mailbox, or if that cannot be checked (this run only). It is the window's form of -AcceptRetentionRisk: it stays ticked for Previews, changing it voids the Preview, and it is cleared once an Apply has run, so it covers one Apply only. The Preview of the Recover reports what the retention check found; tick the box only after reading it (chapter 6).

Why a child process and not the window's own session: a child keeps the cloud modules out of the window (Graph before Exchange Online), keeps the operation atomic (the window cannot be closed mid-batch), leaves the UI thread free, and means that no AD or cloud module is ever imported into the WPF host. The child's output pipes are copied straight to those two files by Stream.CopyToAsync (pure .NET on the thread pool: no PowerShell code ever runs on a background thread, and a child that prints more than a pipe buffer never blocks); the window's timer only reads what has been written so far, through a second read-only stream of the file.

What the console decides for you (3.0.0)

  • The phase. A server that can do the Active Directory side and the cloud side (role AD + Cloud on Setup: RSAT, the cloud programs and Microsoft 365 reachable from this server) runs a new Convert or Recover as Phase Both (the console names it AD and cloud, on this server): everything is done there, there is no transfer package and the Task page says so. The AD phase (which writes a package) or the Cloud phase only appears when the server can do one side only, which includes a server with every program but no access to Microsoft 365 (role AD, amber light, the Setup page says why); Expert mode can still force a phase.
  • Identity. Under the Identity field, Check (also when the field loses the focus or Enter is pressed) shows the account that was resolved (display name, UPN, mailbox type) or says plainly that it was not found or is ambiguous. It is a read-only lookup made by a child process (25 s at most): the window never waits for Active Directory.
  • Run page. A step that works object by object shows 1 / 2 objects with a proportional bar as the objects complete; the steps of the whole batch (Entra Connect, replication, package, cloud wait) are in the journey of every object, marked Whole batch; the card shows the backup of the object. After an Apply, Back no longer leads to the verification (use Start a new task to run again); Open report and Open log are next to the status on the Next steps page, and Open global report when the run produced one.
  • Run settings. Replicate Active Directory before the Entra Connect sync is an ordinary run setting (see Active Directory replication).

Recipe 1 — Convert one user

Nothing to change in the configuration: -Identity replaces the scope (UPN, sAMAccountName, DN or GUID).

PowerShell
cd D:\PRA\PraRemoteMailbox
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Identity jdupont@contoso.com               # 1. preview
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Identity jdupont@contoso.com -Mode Apply   # 2. convert

The preview shows jdupont UserMailbox → RemoteUserMailbox · convert, the attributes that change and licence group … not member → member. The Apply backs up the account, writes AD, adds it to the licence group, runs one Entra Connect cycle, then waits until Exchange Online shows a mailbox and a licence. The summary ends with:

Text
Batch       1d5ac20b
Next        To roll back this batch later: .\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Recover -Batch 1d5ac20b

To undo: recipe 5.

Recipe 2 — Convert a whole OU (users and shared mailboxes)

  1. In config\PraRemoteMailbox.config.psd1, section Scope:
PowerShell
Scope = @{
    Mode                   = 'OU'
    SearchBase             = 'OU=Paris,OU=Sites,DC=contoso,DC=com'   # sub-OUs included
    GroupDN                = ''
    CsvPath                = ''
    IncludeShared          = $true      # also the shared mailboxes of the OU
    IncludeRoom            = $false
    IncludeEquip           = $false
    ExcludeSamAccountNames = @('svc-scan', 'test01')    # never converted
}
  1. Then:
PowerShell
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert                 # preview: every on-premises mailbox of the OU
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Mode Apply     # convert them all, in one batch

Only on-premises mailboxes are taken: objects without an on-premises mailbox (already in Exchange Online, mail users, contacts) are ignored. For a first wave, add -MaxObjects 10 (the first 10 by sAMAccountName). For the shared mailboxes, the preview also lists who will get FullAccess, SendAs and SendOnBehalf (see shared mailbox permissions).

Recipe 3 — Convert only the shared mailboxes

All the shared mailboxes of the configured scope (recipe 2), users excluded — for example a second wave after the users:

PowerShell
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Scope SharedOnly               # preview
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Scope SharedOnly -Mode Apply   # convert

One shared mailbox only:

PowerShell
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Identity compta@contoso.com
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Identity compta@contoso.com -Mode Apply

Shared mailboxes never get a licence. After the sync, the tool waits for the cloud shared mailbox, then grants each permission found in AD and re-reads it; every grant is printed (compta@contoso.com: FullAccess granted to marie@contoso.com and verified). The permission holders do not need to be converted first: a user still on-premises exists in Exchange Online as a synchronised mail user and can receive the permission (it is useful as soon as that user has a cloud mailbox). -Scope SharedOnly takes the shared mailboxes even when IncludeShared = $false; with Scope.Mode = 'Csv', use a file that lists only shared mailboxes. The mirror option is -Scope UsersOnly.

Recipe 4 — Convert a list of mailboxes or the members of a group

Source Configuration (Scope)
A CSV file Mode = 'Csv', CsvPath = '.\config\Wave1.csv' — one column Identity (UPN, sAMAccountName, DN or GUID), see config\Targets.sample.csv. Every line must be an on-premises mailbox, otherwise nothing is converted.
An AD group Mode = 'Group', GroupDN = 'CN=PRA-Wave1,OU=Groups,DC=contoso,DC=com' (nested groups included).

The commands are those of recipe 2. To take a group for one run only, without writing it in the configuration file, give it on the command line (the console does the same with its source AD group):

PowerShell
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Group 'PRA-Wave1'
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Group 'CN=PRA-Wave1,OU=Groups,DC=contoso,DC=com' -Mode Apply

The run says how many members the group has, nested groups included, and lists each member that is not converted with its reason (a computer, a contact, a user without an on-premises mailbox, a shared mailbox when shared mailboxes are not included, an excluded account). An empty group stops with nothing changed.

Recipe 5 — Roll back (Recover)

Use the batch ID of the Convert (summary, report, or the folder name Backups\Batch-<id>…):

PowerShell
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Recover -Batch 1d5ac20b                                       # preview of the roll-back
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Recover -Batch 1d5ac20b -Mode Apply                           # the whole batch
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Recover -Batch 1d5ac20b -Identity jdupont@contoso.com -Mode Apply   # one object of the batch

Users get their original attributes back and leave the licence group. Shared mailboxes are first removed from Exchange Online; their on-premises attributes come back when Exchange Online confirms it (up to Polling.TimeoutMinutes), in the same run. Their on-premises permissions were never changed.

The Preview also checks that the retention policy holds the mailboxes that carry the retention tag; the Apply stops before any change when it does not (see Retention in chapter 6). To go on anyway, for this one run: .\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Recover -Batch 1d5ac20b -Mode Apply -AcceptRetentionRisk.

Recipe 6 — Check, at any time

PowerShell
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Check -Batch 1d5ac20b                          # are the mailboxes of the batch in Exchange Online?
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Check -Identity jdupont@contoso.com             # one mailbox
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Check -Batch 1d5ac20b -Expect Deprovisioned     # after a Recover

Read only. -Batch also takes the ID printed by a Recover: Check then reads the Convert batch that it rolled back (give -Expect Deprovisioned). Check waits for the expected state (up to Polling.TimeoutMinutes); add -Once for a single pass. Each wait line says what is awaited: a mailbox that is still on-premises never reaches the expected state without a Convert, so use -Once for it. A failed Check counts one error. It also shows whether the mailbox carries the X500 addresses recorded by the Convert (section X500 addresses, chapter 2).

Scenario C — Convert on two servers

  1. 1
    AD server
    .\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Phase AD -Mode Apply — backup, AD changes, sync. The summary prints the batch ID.
  2. 2
    Copy
    Copy the two files Backups\Outbox\PRA-<Environment>-Convert-<id8>-for-Cloud.zip and PRA-<Environment>-Convert-<id8>-for-Cloud.zip.sha256 to the cloud server, into the same folder, anywhere. Without the .sha256 file the package is refused. (Copying the whole Batch-<id> folder still works.)
  3. 3
    Cloud server
    .\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Phase Cloud -Batch '<package>.zip' -Mode Apply — verifies and imports the package, waits for the mailboxes, grants the permissions. In the console: Move mailboxes to Exchange Online, Continue, Import package....

Scenario D — Recover on two servers

  1. 1
    Cloud server
    -Action Check -Batch <convert id> -Expect Retained — read only; writes the retention proof (RetentionProof-<batch id>-<time>.json and its .sha256 file) in Backups\Outbox. Copy both files to Backups\Inbox of the AD server (the AD server accepts a proof for as many hours as its own Retention.ProofMaxAgeHours says, 24 by default). Without a proof, when it cannot ask Exchange Online itself, the AD server cannot read the retention and the next step is refused.
  2. 2
    AD server
    -Action Recover -Phase AD -Batch <convert id> -Mode Apply — users restored, shared mailboxes deprovisioned. Exit code 2: next step required.
  3. 3
    Copy
    Copy PRA-<Environment>-Recover-<id8>-for-Cloud.zip and its .sha256 file to the cloud server, into the same folder: the package holds the new Recover batch and the original Convert batch.
  4. 4
    Cloud server
    -Action Recover -Phase Cloud -Batch '<recover package>.zip' -Mode Apply — checks the deprovisioning and writes the Finalize package PRA-<Environment>-Finalize-<id8>-for-AD.zip.
  5. 5
    Copy back
    Copy that zip and its .sha256 file to the AD server.
  6. 6
    AD server
    -Action Finalize -Batch '<finalize package>.zip' -Mode Apply — restores the shared mailboxes and the retention tags.

Since 2.1.0, -Phase Cloud never performs the last AD restore itself, even with RSAT installed. Phase Both retains inline restoration unless DeferOnPremRestore is enabled. Finalize is only required when the result supplies a Finalize package (deferred shared attributes or retention tags).

What you see

  1. The banner: action, mode, scope, tenant, configuration and log file.
  2. Numbered steps. In a preview, the steps that write are shown as skipped.
  3. For each object: its type change (UserMailbox → RemoteUserMailbox) and only the attributes that change — green = added, yellow = changed, red = removed. For a shared mailbox, the holders that will get FullAccess, SendAs and SendOnBehalf in Exchange Online. The full before/after values and the complete lists of holders are in the log.
  4. The summary: result, batch ID, backup, report, log, duration and the next command.

Exit codes

Code Meaning What to do
0 Done (or preview without error): nothing is left to do nothing
1 Failed — see Error in the summary fix the cause, run the same command again — only if nothing was changed yet (the summary says so; the Entra Connect check, the backup and the first error all stop before or at the first write). After the AD changes, go on with the batch (see below)
2 Done, but objects are Pending: a phase AD that ends with a transfer package (the cloud part is still to do), or a sync that did not run (the last line of the log and of the run reads RESULT: PENDING; RESULT: PASS is exit code 0 and RESULT: FAIL exit code 1) run the next step printed in the summary

A Convert or Recover with -Phase AD therefore exits with 2 when it ends with a package: the batch is half done, and the console shows it as "Next step required", not as an error. When the tool did not run the Entra Connect sync (EntraConnect.Sync = $false, or a failure), the first numbered step is Run a delta sync on the server (Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta) or wait for the next automatic cycle (about 30 minutes), before Copy the package.

The Entra Connect sync could not run after the AD changes. The AD part is made and verified, so the run does not fail: the objects are Pending (exit code 2), the transfer package is still written (phase AD) and the Next steps say it plainly: AD is changed and verified. The Entra Connect sync did not run: reason. Run a delta sync on the server (Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta) or wait for the next automatic cycle (about 30 minutes), then carry the package to the cloud server. With phase Both the cloud part is not started (the mailboxes would not appear): run the sync, then continue the batch with -Action Convert -Phase Cloud -Batch <id> (it waits for the mailboxes, up to Polling.TimeoutMinutes). The journal of the batch has a line ADSync / Failed.

Finish the AD side of a batch (-Phase AD -Batch). For a batch whose AD changes are made and verified (it has its State-<id>.json proof) but that has no package or no synchronisation, for instance after a run of an older version that stopped at the sync:

PowerShell
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Phase AD -Mode Apply -Batch 490cc62e

The batch, its backup and its proof are checked in full; the Entra Connect check is made as for a conversion (it stops with nothing written if it fails); the synchronisation runs again; the transfer package is written. Active Directory is not written and the same objects are not converted twice. A Preview shows what would be done. A batch without proof is refused ("cannot be finished from here"). The same command is printed when a conversion is started again for an object that is already converted.

A partial batch. A Convert stops at its first error. The objects verified before it have their AD proof, marked partial (the proof says how many objects were planned). -Phase AD -Batch <id> and -Phase Cloud -Batch <id> accept it: the objects of the proof are continued, and each other object of the backup is reported not converted by this batch (Skipped, one line each, a warning for the batch). The Next steps then say how to convert those objects (fix the cause, then a new Convert for them only: the converted ones are refused by the same command) or how to undo the batch. The object the batch stopped on may be partly changed (a write was started, the batch stopped before it was verified: the journal has a Started or Applied line for it). It is not in the list of objects to convert again: it is reported may be partly changed (Pending), and the Next steps give the rollback (-Action Recover -Batch <id>, Preview first), which restores it. The objects that were never touched are Skipped.

-Action Recover -Batch <id> of a partial batch takes only the objects of the proof and the object the batch stopped on; every other object of the backup is reported Skipped ("not converted by this batch": nothing to roll back), so an object that another batch converted since is not rolled back by this one. -Action Check -Batch <id> of a partial batch reports the objects that were never converted as not as expected.

New Convert for the objects that are left. With -CsvPath, the Next steps give a command with a CSV file that lists only the objects still to convert (same columns as your file, written in the log folder); with -Identity, -SearchBase or -Group the command keeps the filters: the converted objects are not eligible any more and are skipped. On the cloud server the AD-side commands are introduced by On the AD server: and are written without this server's configuration path.

A Convert batch that a Recover rolled back, or started to roll back, cannot be resumed (-Phase AD -Batch and the cloud phase refuse it: "Convert batch X cannot be resumed: Recover batch Y already rolled back objects of it"). A Recover that stopped before its proof counts too: its journal tells which objects it had started on; a journal that is missing counts for every object. On two servers the cloud server learns of the Recover only when the Recover package has been imported there: until then it cannot refuse.

Chapter 9

Reading the results

In short: Every run writes a report that opens in a browser. Read the result, then the warnings, then the line of each person.

The HTML report

One page per run in reports\: tiles with the counters (including Warnings), the next step, the warnings of the run, one row per object, and the run errors. It is self-contained (no external resource, no network, no telemetry).

The rows are stored in the page as compressed chunks of 20,000 rows (gzip, then base64: compression, not encryption; protect the file like the CSV). When the page opens it decodes all chunks at once (eager, not lazy; about 0.3 s for 50,000 rows on the test PC), then shows only the rows in view: the Summary grid (the eight columns above) and the All 22 fields grid never hold more than 200 data rows in the page, whatever the number of rows. Scroll, or use the keyboard (arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End, Enter for all the fields of a row). Filters (status, type, action, six yes/no flags, ten text fields and a search over the 22 fields) combine with AND, always inspect every row and show the filtered counts; Reset filters clears them. Export filtered CSV writes every matching row with the 22 fields (semicolon, UTF-8 with BOM, every field quoted, a cell starting with =, +, - or @ gets a leading '). The CSV written next to the report is unchanged and has the raw values. Warnings and run errors are listed 100 per page with their own filter; none is dropped.

Requirement: a current desktop Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome (the page needs DecompressionStream). Without it, without JavaScript, or if a chunk is missing or damaged, the page says so explicitly and displays no partial result; the run summary (tiles, next step) stays visible and the CSV with the same name holds every row. A report of 50,000 or 100,000 rows is for reading; Apply itself remains designed for the batch sizes of the guide.

The global report (two servers, one report)

With two servers, each side writes its own report (as before). The last server also writes ONE global report that follows every object from the first server to the last, for Convert (AD, then Cloud) as for Recover (AD, Cloud, then Finalize), whatever the type of the objects (users, shared mailboxes, all):

  • How the data travels. Each side that hands over to another, and the cloud phase that ends a Convert, keeps what it did in two files inside the batch folder (the batch folder it creates, or the Convert batch folder for the cloud phase of a Convert). PhaseData-<time>-<phase>-<run>.json holds the run (server, operator account, start and end, mode, tool version, the run settings that differ from the configuration file, the steps, the name of the run log) and one entry per object (readable name, type, final status, warnings, backup path). PhaseEvents-<time>-<phase>-<run>.jsonl holds, one JSON object per line, the steps of every object (status, time, message), the journey lines that name no object, the errors and the warnings. Each file has its .sha256, and the PhaseData file carries the SHA-256 of its events file, so that an events file that is swapped or changed is not used. Both files are in the transfer package, listed in transfer.json with their SHA-256 like every entry: a package whose phase data was changed is refused at import. The Finalize package also carries the earlier phases (Recover on the AD server, the original Convert as history). Phase data written by an earlier version (the steps inside the one JSON file) is still read.
  • What is written. On the run that ends the chain (Both, the cloud phase of a Convert, the Finalize, a Recover cloud phase that needs no Finalize), in reports\: PRA_<run>.global.html and three CSV files next to the usual per-phase files: .global.csv (one line per object: Verdict, Sides, Note, BackupPath, EventCount, RunSettings...), .global.events.csv (one line per journey line: object, phase, step, status, time, message) and .global.issues.csv (one line per error or warning). The CSV files hold everything: no object, no journey line and no error or warning is left out of them. The page keeps its data compressed and shows it a piece at a time, so that it stays usable for thousands of objects. The summary is plain HTML: the totals, the side that is not available, what was left out (see below), the errors and warnings per phase, the batch timeline (each phase: server, operator, times, duration, status, mode, tool) and the run settings changed per phase. The objects are in a grid that keeps at most 200 rows in the page, with a search, a filter on the verdict and on the type, and the count of each verdict in the filter; a click (or Enter) on an object opens its journey in pages of 100 lines (side, step, status, time, message, the result of each phase last); the errors and warnings are in pages of 100 with a filter; the Export buttons give the filtered objects, or their journeys, as CSV. Adding #object=<name or object GUID> (any letter case) to the address opens a journey. Verdicts: done, done with warnings, failed, pending, skipped. An object present on one side only is shown explicitly (for example filtered out on the cloud side: pending, with the reason). Times are UTC. The page contains no external resource and needs a current desktop Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome to show its data; without script it still shows the summary, and the CSV files hold the rest. The console opens it from Next steps (Open global report); the CLI result has GlobalHtmlReport, GlobalCsvReport, GlobalEventsCsvReport and GlobalIssuesCsvReport, and the Next steps name their paths.
  • Nothing is cut silently. What a limit leaves out is counted in the header of the phase data and shown in the card Not everything was kept of the page, with the phase, the count and where the complete data is (the log of that run, named in the card with the machine that wrote it). The limits are: more than 200,000 objects in one phase; more than 1,000,000 journey lines in one phase; a text longer than 300 characters (a step) or 2,000 characters (a detail), which ends with ...; objects that would take the PhaseData file of a phase above 64 MB (the last objects of the list are left out, counted in the card, and their journey lines stay in the events file under their name); lines that would take the events file of a phase above 96 MB. An events file above 96 MB (or that, with the others read for the same report, would take more than 96 MB), and a PhaseData file above 256 MB (a file of 3.1.x holds its steps itself and has no events file; it is read up to that size), is reported as not read: the card says why and the phase is shown without its steps, errors and warnings. What to do: the complete data is in the log of that run (named in the card); to report on the phase anyway, move the PhaseData and PhaseEvents files of other phases out of the batch folder (the 96 MB is for all the events files of one report) and run the same command again. An events file that is missing, changed, without its .sha256 or unreadable is not used: the phase is shown without its steps, errors and warnings, and the card says why. A line of an events file that is longer than 65,536 characters or is not a JSON object is skipped and counted. Errors and warnings have no limit: every one is in the page, in the issues CSV and in the counts of the plain summary. At most 200 PhaseData files of a folder are read for one report, the newest first, and the report says how many older ones were not read.
  • Older batches, folders copied by hand. Without phase data (or with a file that fails its checksum, its schema or its Environment) the report is still written, and the missing side is listed as not available (folder from an older version or copied manually); the verdicts then come from the sides that were carried.
  • Privacy. Names, statuses and messages only: no secret, no token. The plain summary is HTML-encoded and the page script shows every value as text, never as markup; spreadsheet formulas are neutralised in the CSV; the files are private like the other reports and backups.
  • The .sha256 next to a PhaseData file is an integrity check, not proof of origin: the protection against a changed file is the SHA-256 of every entry in transfer.json, verified at import; the report decides nothing from this data. The console only reads the header of a PhaseData file, to label a batch (cloud part done, pending, stopped, handed over), and only when its .sha256 matches the file and the file names the batch of its folder and the Environment of that batch; a file that fails one of these counts as no data, and a file that cannot be opened just now is read again at the next refresh.
  • A cloud part completed by a later run. When the cloud part of a phase Both run failed (objects not ready in time) and -Phase Cloud -Batch <id> completed it, the verdict of the object follows the later run: the cloud error of the earlier run stays in its journey as an Earlier run line and does not make the object failed.
  • Phase Both uses the same layout (one phase). The per-phase HTML report also lists the run settings changed (the per-phase CSV keeps its 22 columns).

Warnings

A warning never stops the run and never changes the exit code; it says that something was left aside on purpose and should be read. Today: the permission entries of a shared mailbox that point to an account no longer in AD or that is not a user or a group, and the Deny entries that are not reproduced (chapter 2); the objects that a Recover finds changed since the batch left them, and the retention that a Recover accepted or did not check (chapter 6); and an X500 address missing in Exchange Online (chapter 2, X500 addresses). It is shown in four places: a yellow ▲ line in the console under the object, [WARN] in the log, the Warnings column of the CSV, and in the HTML report (Warnings tile, Warnings card, yellow mark on the row). The summary card of the console turns yellow and shows the last warnings.

Statuses

FinalStatus Meaning
Planned Preview: this is what Apply would do.
Success Done and verified (AD re-read; cloud state reached).
AlreadyDone Nothing to change: the object was already in the expected state (counted as done).
Pending AD done, waiting for another step (shared mailbox deprovisioning, Finalize, the Exchange Online part of phase Both), or not reached because the run stopped (an error, or a stop from outside).
Error Stopped; see Detail and the log.
Skipped Not processed: no applicable check, or not converted by a partial batch (it stopped at its first error before this object).

The CSV columns

ObjectGuid, SamAccountName, UserPrincipalName, Action, IsShared, ADApplied (an AD write was made), ADVerified (AD re-read matches), GroupAction (Added / Removed / Preserved), BackupPath, LastOperation, CloudMailbox, CloudLicense, CloudStatus, CloudDetail, PreserveCloudMailbox, PreserveLicense, DeprovisionConfirmed, PermDetail (permissions verified / to grant / trustees missing), PermMissing, FinalStatus, Detail, Warnings (e.g. permission entries ignored). Separator ;, UTF-8.

Caution

Logs, transcripts and reports contain AD values (addresses, DNs). Protect them like the backups; never publish them unfiltered.

Chapter 10

Files: batches, proofs and packages

In short: Every move is a folder with a backup and a proof. Between two servers, one zip file carries it, with its .sha256 file.

Text
Backups\
  Batch-efb9d60a75054b6b9cabefa418121934\          one batch = one Apply (private ACL)
    Recover-LAB-20260930_194723-efb9d60a.json       typed records: what is restored (schema 3)
    Recover-LAB-20260930_194723-efb9d60a.json.sha256
    Recover-LAB-20260930_194723-efb9d60a.clixml     every AD value of every object (data-only CLIXML)
    State-efb9d60a75054b6b9cabefa418121934.json     AD proof: objects verified after the writes (+ .sha256)
    Journal-efb9d60a75054b6b9cabefa418121934.jsonl  Started / Applied / Verified / Failed per write
  Finalize-3f2c90e1....\                           Finalize package (Recover on two servers)
  <RunId>-cloud\CloudOperations.jsonl              journal of the Exchange Online grants of a run
  Outbox\PRA-<Env>-<Kind>-<id8>-for-<Cloud|AD>.zip  transfer package written at each handover (+ .sha256)
  Inbox\                                           packages dropped here are listed by the console
logs\     PRA_<RunId>_<n>.log  and  .transcript.txt
reports\  PRA_<RunId>_<n>.csv  and  .html
  • Batch ID = the first 8 characters of the folder name; -Batch accepts 8 characters or more, or the path of the JSON file.
  • The State file is the proof that the AD part was done and verified: the cloud phase and Finalize refuse to write without it.
  • Carry one transfer package (the zip and its .sha256 file, below) between the servers; if you copy folders by hand instead, copy whole folders, never single files, and never rename them.
  • Keep the batches at least until the Recover is finished and checked; then archive them with the logs.

The transfer package (one zip file, with its checksum file, from one server to the other)

At each handover of a two-server run (Convert or Recover with -Phase AD, and the cloud phase of a Recover that needs a final AD restore), an Apply writes one zip file and its .sha256 file in <Storage.BackupFolder>\Outbox\ (a private folder like the backups), named after its purpose:

File Written by To carry to
PRA-<Environment>-Convert-<id8>-for-Cloud.zip Convert -Phase AD the cloud server
PRA-<Environment>-Recover-<id8>-for-Cloud.zip Recover -Phase AD (the new Recover batch and the original Convert batch) the cloud server
PRA-<Environment>-Finalize-<id8>-for-AD.zip Recover -Phase Cloud (the Finalize package) the AD server

A Preview with -Batch <package.zip> verifies the package and reads it from a private temporary folder under logs\, deleted at the end: nothing is written to the backup folder. The console imports a package off its window thread (a child process, with a busy state), bound to the Environment of the configuration (a package made for another Environment is refused, as on the command line), and extracts it through a staging folder renamed into place.

Each package also carries the phase data of the side that wrote it (the PhaseData file and its events file, see The global report), in the batch folder, listed and hashed like every other entry.

Each package is a standard ZIP (System.IO.Compression, entries in a fixed order) with its checksum file <name>.zip.sha256 next to it. It holds the batch folders the other side needs (JSON, data-only CLIXML, .sha256 files, State proof, Finalize manifest) under their own folder names, and a transfer.json manifest: schema version, kind, Environment, creation time, tool version, the name, size and SHA-256 of every entry and the next command. The folders in Backups\ are written as before: they stay the source of truth, and copying the folders by hand still works exactly as in 2.x. The summary and the console say: copy these two files (the zip and its .sha256 file) to the cloud (or AD) server, into the same folder, anywhere you like. A package whose .sha256 file is missing is refused with the name of the file to copy.

Importing is -Batch <package.zip> on the command line (a path, or the bare name of a file waiting in Backups\Inbox, Backups\Outbox or the current folder) or Import package... in the console. The package is verified completely before anything is written:

  • the .sha256 file is present and equals the SHA-256 of the ZIP; transfer.json is present once, well formed, of a known kind and of the same Environment as the configuration;
  • every entry is exactly transfer.json or <Batch-...|Finalize-...>/<file>: a path, a separator other than that one, .., a drive, a rooted or UNC name, a control character, a trailing dot or space, a reserved device name, an unexpected or duplicated name is refused (zip-slip), and so is a manifest entry that is missing;
  • declared sizes equal the real ones, and the totals are bounded (at most 2000 entries, 2 GB per entry, 4 GB in all: room for a batch of 5,000 objects): a compression bomb is refused before it is read, with the message the content is too large or an entry is too large;
  • the SHA-256 of every entry is computed from the stream and compared to the manifest, before the first byte is written.

Then each folder is extracted under Storage.BackupFolder with its original name, as a private folder (leaf-only ACL, like the backups). A folder that already exists with identical files is accepted (importing twice is harmless, and so is running the cloud phase again from the same package); the files that a run writes into a batch folder afterwards (the proof State-*, the journal Journal-*, the report data PhaseData-* and PhaseEvents-*, and the .sha256 files) are kept as they are and are never replaced or supplied by a package; a folder with any different or missing file of the package, or any other extra file, is refused, and nothing is left half-extracted. The normal flow then continues and every proof and hash check of the engine is unchanged: the package replaces the copy of the folders, not the verifications.

PowerShell
.\Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 -Action Convert -Phase Cloud -Mode Apply -Batch 'PRA-PROD-Convert-490cc62e-for-Cloud.zip'

Batch size

A batch of 5,000 objects is supported. The checks that grew with the square of the batch (the backup fingerprint recomputed for every write, the searches of the whole batch for each object, the console reading every batch file at every refresh) are gone: what is done for one object costs the same in a batch of 50 and in a batch of 5,000.

  • The backup is written once and read back once in full (the same pass validates the file and compares it with what was captured), with the SHA-256 of its files. Writing and reading the data-only CLIXML is the work that remains and it is linear: about 0.2 s per object for the whole backup, measured on a loaded workstation with synthetic users of 45 attributes (an object of your directory with more attributes costs more). Plan on roughly 18 minutes for the backup of 5,000 objects, and about 8 minutes each time a server reads the batch for the first time (the cloud server, Finalize).
  • Each write checks the fields of the backup, the record of the object and the length and last write time of the files; the complete check runs when the backup is read, after every 200 such checks and before the AD proof is written. The AD proof is read in full once per run by the cloud phase; each permission grant then costs a comparison of stamps.
  • The Active Directory part, the Entra Connect wait and the Exchange Online wait are not made faster by this: the AD part reads and re-reads each object several times (each write is preceded and followed by a read of the object), and the Entra Connect and Exchange Online waits are those of the services. The licence group is not read in full for each object: whether an object is a member comes from its own memberOf attribute, and a group of thousands of members is read once for the objects of a run. On the synthetic data, planning takes about 0.05 s per object, the AD part about 0.2 s per object after the backup (about 18 minutes for 5,000 objects), and reading the AD proof and the per-object checks of the cloud phase about 14 minutes for 5,000 objects.
  • The console keeps what it read of each batch file while the file and its .sha256 file are unchanged, so a refresh costs a listing of the folder. A reload after a new batch reads that batch only. A failure to read a file (a lock) is never kept, and the Reload link forgets everything the window kept about batch files and CSV files.
  • The bounds that remain: a transfer package is refused above 2 GB for one entry and 4 GB in all (with the message too large); a phase keeps at most 200,000 objects and 1,000,000 journey lines, and drops no error or warning; the global report holds every object, every journey line and every error and warning, and names in a card what a limit left out; one events file, and all the events files of one report together, are at most 96 MB (measured on synthetic data: an events file of 50 MB, 141,000 lines for 5,000 objects, is read in about 50 s with 1.2 GB of memory, and the whole global report takes about 105 s and 3.3 GB; the memory is about 65 times the size of the events files, so the limit keeps the report within about 6 GB); a PhaseData file is read up to 256 MB (the writer keeps at most 64 MB) and the PhaseData files read for one report at most 256 MB together (a file that would pass it is not read: the report says so and gives the command to run again after the files of other batches are moved out of the batch folder). A Convert that sent permission grants (phase Cloud or Both) ends its grant work with one complete check of the backup.
  • The global report, measured at 5,000 objects with 12 journey lines each (synthetic data, one workstation): writing the phase data takes about 20 s (2.8 MB for the header and the objects, 14 MB for the events file), and the report about 52 s (the model, a page of 0.6 MB and three CSV files of 1.6 MB, 15 MB and 0.03 MB). Version 3.1.4 took about 16 s and 84 s for a page of 18 MB with one table row for each journey line. In the browser the page keeps about 1,300 elements whatever the number of objects (at most 200 grid rows, 100 error rows and 100 journey rows), and decodes its data in a fraction of a second.
  • tools\Measure-PraScale.ps1 times these steps on synthetic data (no directory, no tenant, no network): pwsh -File .\tools\Measure-PraScale.ps1 -Count 5000. Run the heavy steps (BackupSave, AdBatch, ProofImport) with a smaller -Count first: they take hours at 5,000.
Part IVMaintain
Chapter 11

Inside the tool

In short: For developers: the order of the steps and the safety rules that no option can skip.

Execution flow

Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox
action, mode, phase
PRA.Commonconfig, audit, console
PRA.Directory
plans, backup, AD writes
PRA.BackupCLIXML capture
PRA.Cloud
EXO, Graph, grants

The run state is one hashtable, the context ($context), created by the entry script and passed to every function: configuration, mode, the result rows, the run errors (Issues), the files produced, the current step, and two callbacks: Approval (ShouldProcess before every write) and, in the cloud phase, AssertCloudAuthorization (re-reads the AD proof before every Exchange Online grant).

The safety contract

  1. Read everything, then write. Every object of the batch is read and planned before the first write.
  2. Backup before the first write, for the whole batch: typed JSON (what Recover restores), data-only CLIXML (every AD value), SHA-256, private folder, new files only, then re-read and compared with the plans. A failure at the 13th object stops before any write.
  3. Before each write: no previous error, Apply mode, approval, backup unchanged (for each write: the fields of the backup in memory, the record of the object, and the length and last write time of its three files; the complete check, every record and the SHA-256 of the files, runs when the backup is read, after every 200 such checks and before the proof is written), and the object re-read: same uSNChanged, same DN, same values as in the backup. After each write: re-read of the expected values.
  4. First error = stop: no next object, no sync, no cloud write, no automatic rollback. The journal records Started before and Applied after every write.
  5. Proofs: the State file lists the objects verified; the cloud phase, Finalize and the sync refuse a batch without a valid proof, and Finalize refuses an object changed since the proof. One change is accepted: the writeback of Entra Connect, when the X500: addresses of proxyAddresses are the only difference from the list of the proof and every other managed attribute is as the proof left it (the list of kept addresses is then computed again).
  6. A cloud error is never "absent": deprovisioning is confirmed only when Exchange Online returns no mailbox and a MailUser recipient. Only then are the shared mailboxes restored on-premises.
  7. Preview and Check never write (AD, Entra Connect, Exchange Online); they still write their log, transcript and report.
  8. Strings are compared ordinally. On PowerShell 7 (.NET, ICU) the usual comparison operators ignore zero-width and control characters ("a" -ceq "a<U+0001>" is true). Every comparison that guards integrity, identity or authorisation (hashes, GUIDs, Environment, Operation, file names, the RawFormat marker, codec type and XML names, trustees, the typed confirmation) is ordinal; a character that does not belong refuses the object instead of matching it. Ordinal does not mean case sensitive: every value an operator types or picks (parameters, configuration values, CSV columns and values, group, batch, folder and package names, addresses, Environment) ignores the letter case; hashes may be written in either case, and the case of the SMTP: prefix keeps its meaning (primary address). See the pitfalls table (chapter 12) and the limitations note below.

Limitations of the ordinal comparison. The ordinal rule applies to the runtime files of the package; the tests, the tools and the display-only sorts (lists shown in the window, the OU picker) keep the usual operators. ValidateSet still uses the culture comparison: the entry script and the window request refuse a value that has no ordinal match. Lists that the tool writes in a canonical order (permission holders, multi-valued attributes, batch order) are now sorted ordinally (upper-case before lower-case, by UTF-16 code unit), which can differ from the order written by 2.x under Windows PowerShell 5.1; the comparison of two states sorts both sides, so old backups still compare equal. Regular expressions are anchored with \z (not $, which also accepts a trailing line feed).

Code map

File Content
Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1 Parameters, context, the four actions step by step, batch resolution (Get-PraBatchFile), one confirmation (Confirm-PraApply), Finalize package (Save-PraFinalizePackage, Get-PraFinalizeInput), the transfer package at each handover (Publish-PraTransferPackage) and its import by -Batch <zip> (Resolve-PraTransferPackagePath), the plan of steps, next-step hints.
PraRemoteMailbox.psd1, PraRemoteMailbox.psm1 Module manifest (ModuleVersion, GUID, PowerShellVersion 7.5, explicit FunctionsToExport, no wildcard) and root module (package check, then PRA.Common and PRA.Directory). PRA.Cloud stays on demand (Graph before Exchange Online in the dedicated process) and PRA.Gui is for -Gui only.
module\PRA.Common.psm1 1 console theme · 2 console and log (Write-PraBanner/Step/Item/Log/Summary) · 3 configuration (Import-PraConfiguration, defaults = list of valid keys; New-PraEffectiveConfiguration writes the effective copy of one run) · 4 audit (log + transcript) · 5 results (Get-PraOutcome, CSV/HTML, Complete-PraRun) · transfer packages (New-, Get- and Import-PraTransferPackage: ZIP, manifest, verification before any write) · events (Write-PraEvent, Write-PraProgress).
module\PRA.Directory.psm1 1 receipts and files · 2 directory reads (Get-PraTarget, Get-PraUser) · 3 attribute states and before/after display · 4 shared permissions from AD · 5 plans (New-PraPlan) · 6 backups and proofs · 7 writes (Invoke-PraAdBatch) · 8 Entra Connect (Invoke-PraSync).
module\PRA.Backup.psm1 Data-only CLIXML codec (write, stream-validate).
module\PRA.Cloud.psm1 Exchange Online worker (fixed commands, identity checks), sessions, pre-check, cloud phase (polling, grants), retention check.
module\PRA.Gui.psm1, module\PRA.Gui.xaml The console: five pages (layout and Fluent theme in the XAML), real prerequisite detection, run settings and their effective configuration, task and batch/package lists, preview guard, confirmation, child-process supervision (cloud child: own console, STARTUPINFOEX with a handle list so that only its three pipe ends are inherited), and the run model built from the PRA_EVENT_FILE events (plan, step, item, progress, result). Notifying rows are ExpandoObjects: no compiled helper type.
module\PRA.Gui.Directory.ps1 Read-only OU list for the window, run in a separate PowerShell 7 process (AD only, no write).
module\Test-PackageIntegrity.ps1 Package verifier, run by the entry, the root module, every module and the GUI helper before they do anything.

Environment variables read by the tool (all optional):

Variable Use
PRA_ICONS Emoji, Symbols or Ascii: force the console icon set (the window sets Ascii for its child).
PRA_ANSI 1: colours as ANSI sequences (console captures for the documentation).
PRA_EVENT_FILE Path of the JSONL event file; set by the window, it makes the engine emit start, plan, step, item, progress, summary and result events (the console builds its steps, waits and next steps from them).
PRA_STOP_FILE Reserved name, not read by the engine in this version; the window removes it from the child's environment so that an inherited value can never matter.
Chapter 12

Modifying the tool

In short: For developers: where to change the code to manage one more attribute, another address or a new check.

The rule: change the plan, never the guards. The backup, the re-reads and the proofs work for any attribute listed in the plan.

Manage one more AD attribute

  1. Add it to $script:AttributeKinds in PRA.Directory.psm1 with its type (String, MultiString, Bytes, Bool, Int, Long).
  2. Set its target value in New-PraPlan (branch Convert, and Deprovision if needed). Recover restores it automatically from the backup.
  3. Old batches do not contain it: Assert-PraStoredRecord refuses them for Recover. Decide explicitly (new backup schema, or keep old batches on the previous version).
  4. Add a gate test (chapter 13) with a synthetic user having and not having the attribute.

Change the routing address or the recipient types

Get-PraRoutingAddress (routing) and the Convert branch of New-PraPlan (types). Keep msExchRemoteRecipientType of shared mailboxes at 97/99: 100/102 mean "already migrated" and are refused.

Add a cloud check

In Invoke-PraCloudPhase (PRA.Cloud.psm1): add the fact in Get-PraGraphFact or in the worker (Mailbox, Recipient), then include it in $mbok / $licok. A new Exchange Online write must go through Invoke-PraPermissionGrant (approval, proof, journal, one call, bounded re-read).

Change the console or the report

Texts and icons: PRA.Common.psm1, region 1-2. The HTML report: templates\Report.template.html (markers {{...}}; the data is written by Write-PraReportHtml, which fills {{DATA}}; no change of the data format without changing the viewer script). The template is covered by the package integrity check. The CSV columns: $script:RowFields.

PowerShell pitfalls met during the build

Pitfall Rule
The Windows PowerShell 5.1 transcript (2.x) wrote every Write-Host -NoNewline piece on its own line (kept as a rule: the transcript stays readable in every host) one Write-Host per line, one colour per line (Write-PraHost)
PowerShell 7 on .NET (ICU) compares strings with the culture collation, which ignores zero-weight characters: -eq, -ceq, -ne, -cne, -in, -cin, -contains, -like, switch, Group-Object, Select-Object -Unique, Sort-Object, .StartsWith(string), .EndsWith(string), .IndexOf(string) and hash tables built on a culture comparer treat "a" and "a<U+0001>" as equal. Regular expressions, .Contains(string), [string]::Equals and the default Dictionary / HashSet are ordinal. for a hash, an identity, a name or a mode: Test-PraOrdinalEqual, Test-PraOrdinalIgnoreCaseEqual, Test-PraOrdinalIn, Get-PraOrdinalSorted, Get-PraOrdinalUnique (PRA.Common) or an explicit [StringComparison]::Ordinal / OrdinalIgnoreCase; never -ceq, -cne, -cin, -cnotin (a test refuses them in the runtime files)
GetNewClosure() copies the variables of the current scope, including parameters with validation attributes (an empty [ValidateSet] parameter throws) create closures inside a small function (New-PraApprovalCallback)
ShouldProcess reads $ConfirmPreference of the calling scope the approval closure sets it from $context.ConfirmPreference
App-only Exchange Online sessions report the organisation domain as TenantID the session guard accepts Cloud.Organization + AppId
Import-Module ActiveDirectory creates an AD: drive on a default DC $env:ADPS_LoadDefaultDrive = 0 before the import
Files without BOM are read as ANSI by Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the BOM also makes an accidental run under 5.1 stop at #Requires with a readable message) every .ps1/.psm1/.psd1 is UTF-8 with BOM (checked by the gate)
ConvertFrom-Json of PowerShell 7 turns ISO 8601 strings into [DateTime] (CapturedUtc, CreatedUtc, Utc), so the byte-exact comparisons of the proofs fail every read goes through ConvertFrom-PraJson (-DateKind String, PowerShell 7.5+); a test refuses any other ConvertFrom-Json in package\
[IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory(path, security) and GetAccessControl(path) do not exist on .NET [IO.FileSystemAclExtensions]::Create / GetAccessControl on a DirectoryInfo (the folder is still created with its private ACL)
Export-Csv -Encoding UTF8 writes no BOM in PowerShell 7 (Excel then reads the ; CSV as ANSI) -Encoding utf8BOM for the CSV report
Get-ADUser -Identity does not search the UPN exact, escaped LDAP filter (Get-PraUser)
With -ErrorAction Stop, Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes a TerminatingError line in the transcript even when the error is caught and expected (e.g. "No permissions were found" before a FullAccess grant) read an expected error through -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -ErrorVariable and check every record; anything else is thrown
Get-EXORecipient -UserPrincipalName answers an absent object with HTTP 404 (ManagementObjectNotFoundException), not with an empty result only that exact answer, for that exact UPN, means "absent" (MissingRecipient); any other error stops
Exchange Online assemblies stay loaded in the console after a run; Microsoft Graph loaded later fails (GetTokenAsync ... does not have an implementation) Graph is connected before EXO within a run; between runs, a clear message asks for a new window
Chapter 13

Testing a change

In short: The test gate runs without a directory or a tenant. Run it after every change.

The gate (no directory, no tenant)

PowerShell
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tests\Invoke-TestGate.ps1   # in the repository; tests and tools are not part of the package

It checks every file (parse, UTF-8 BOM, help), runs PSScriptAnalyzer (PowerShell 7 compatibility profiles), then the Pester suites tests\PraRemoteMailbox.Tests.ps1, tests\PraRemoteMailbox.Gui.Tests.ps1, tests\PackageIntegrity.Tests.ps1, tests\PraReport.Tests.ps1 and tests\PraDocumentation.Tests.ps1 (the documentation suite checks pictures, names, the Graph scope and readability; the integrity logic on a controlled copy where only the signature call is substituted, plus the real package, which fails closed unless every file carries the valid owner signature): synthetic AD and ADSync modules, a synthetic cloud barrier, the real entry script in a separate PowerShell 7 process, and the WPF window without live connections. It proves in particular: no write before the complete backup, stop at the first error, no write in Preview/-WhatIf, no Apply without confirmation in a non-interactive process, memory bounds with 13 shared mailboxes × 500 trustees, proofs and Finalize packages, GUI phase/command boundaries and preview invalidation. Evidence: tests\evidence\gate\<date>\ (RESULT.txt, gate-result.json, Pester XML).

Requirements: Pester 5 or later and PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0 (machine-wide modules). Every test is mandatory: a skipped or missing test fails the gate.

Release 3.0.0 (2026-11-05, signed and timestamped, PowerShell 7.5+): 764 tests, 764 passed, 0 analyzer error, about 80 minutes under pwsh 7.6 (the analyzer lists 1263 non-error diagnostics, among them the 7.5 additions that the PowerShell 7.0 profiles do not know). The gate of 2.3.0 under Windows PowerShell 5.1 was 506 tests; the extra tests are the PowerShell 7 engine, the review fixes, the 54 tests of the ordinal comparisons (tag Ordinal), the replay of the 2.2.0 fixtures and the 25 tests of the documentation (tests\PraDocumentation.Tests.ps1: pictures, private names, permissions against the code, readability of the user guide).

Release 2.3.0 (2026-11-03, unreleased source, working tree not yet signed): 506 tests, 506 passed, 0 analyzer error; the native-state test accepts the fail-closed state of the unsigned package. Run the gate from a Windows PowerShell whose PSModulePath does not start with the PowerShell 7 module folders (the tests start powershell.exe children that inherit it).

Release 2.0.0 (2026-10-01, VMLLM): 279 tests, 279 passed, 0 analyzer error, about 12 minutes — evidence tests\evidence\gate\v2.0.0-release. The only analyzer warnings on the delivered files are expected: Write-Host in the console module (14, by design) and ConvertFrom-Markdown in the documentation builder (6, PowerShell 7 tool). Compared with the 325 tests of 1.3.6, the 61 combinations of the removed path options (-BackupFile, -StateFile, -LogPath, -TranscriptPath, -ReportDirectory) are replaced by 9 tests of -Batch and of the confirmation.

The documentation and its pictures

Two guides: the user guide (PraRemoteMailbox-UserGuide.md, plain words, one picture per step) and this reference guide. Both are built into one HTML file each, with a light and a dark theme:

PowerShell
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\New-DocumentationImages.ps1   # every picture, then the two HTML guides (needs Microsoft Edge)
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Build-Documentation.ps1       # only the HTML guides (the pictures are embedded)

No picture is drawn by hand. tools\New-DocumentationImages.ps1 rebuilds them all from the repository: the console is the real window (PRA.Gui.psm1) driven against a synthetic engine (tools\DocumentationImages\Show-ConsoleScreens.ps1 and StubEngine.ps1), with numbered callouts on what the operator clicks; the reports come from the real report code on synthetic phase data; the diagrams use the CSS of the built guides. The data is synthetic only (contoso.com, SRV-PRA01, CONTOSO\pra.operator, D:\PRA\PraRemoteMailbox, D:\PRA\Backups); the console harness stops if a real machine name, user name or local path reaches a window. Run it again after any change of the console, of the reports or of the guides, then commit the pictures with the guides. The suite tests\PraDocumentation.Tests.ps1 checks that every picture used exists, has an alternative text and is in the integrity inventory, that no real name appears, that the documented Graph scope is the one of the code, and that the Start here part of the user guide stays short and simple.

The lab campaign

After a change of the engine, repeat the campaign of annex B on the lab: Preview, Convert Apply (users + shared), Check, Recover on two servers (AD, Cloud with Finalize package, Finalize), plus a Recover of a batch written by the previous version.
