Troubleshooting

In short: The message you see, its cause, and what to do. The user guide, chapter 7 (file PraRemoteMailbox-UserGuide.html) has the same in plainer words.

Message Cause What to do
Configuration: unknown setting X typing mistake or setting of another version compare with chapter 6
Batch <id> not found under ... the batch folder is not in Storage.BackupFolder copy the whole Batch-... / Finalize-... folder there, or give the path of the JSON file
Recover stopped before any change: the retention policy does not hold N mailbox(es) and M could not be checked the retention check before a Recover (chapter 6): a mailbox that carries the retention tag is not held by the policy, or Exchange Online could not be read, or Retention.PolicyGuid is empty nothing was changed. Run the read-only -Action Check -Batch <id> -Expect Retained (the Next steps give it), fix the policy or the PolicyGuid, and run the Preview again. To go on anyway for one run, add -AcceptRetentionRisk to the Apply
No retention proof stands in for the check: … (warning of a Recover, AD part, on a server that cannot ask Exchange Online) the proof written by the Check on the cloud server is missing, older than Retention.ProofMaxAgeHours, dated in the future (the clocks of the two servers differ), of another batch, copy of the batch file, Environment or policy, damaged (its SHA-256 does not match its .sha256 file, an entry is not valid, an object is listed twice), or does not cover every object run the Check -Batch <id> -Expect Retained of the Next steps on the cloud server, copy the two RetentionProof-… files to Backups\Inbox of this server, then run the Preview again. -AcceptRetentionRisk is the last resort
N of the M object(s) changed since this batch left them (warning) a Recover found attributes that are neither as the Convert left them nor as they were before it (an address added during the disaster, a later Convert of the same object) read the PLANNED values of the objects named above: the saved values are put back over what is there now. Nothing is blocked
The Convert batch used by this Recover is not in ... cloud phase of a Recover without the original Convert batch copy the Batch-<convert id> folder too
Batch ... is a Convert batch: the cloud phase of a Recover needs the batch printed by its AD phase wrong ID use the ID printed by Recover -Phase AD
EntraConnect.Sync = $true but the ADSync module is not on this server AD part not on the Entra Connect server set EntraConnect.Server, or run on the Entra Connect server, or Sync = $false
Entra Connect sync will not be possible: this account has no right on X ... the check made before the first AD write was refused: the account cannot open a remote session on X, or cannot use ADSync there give the account Remote Management Users (or Administrators) and ADSyncOperators on X, or set EntraConnect.Sync = $false and synchronise by hand. Nothing was changed
Entra Connect sync will not be possible: X does not answer to PowerShell remoting wrong name in EntraConnect.Server, WinRM (TCP 5985) closed, firewall fix the name or the access (Test-WSMan X shows the network part only). Nothing was changed
AD is changed and verified. The Entra Connect sync did not run: ... (Pending, exit code 2) the check passed, then the cycle failed (right removed, server down, timeout, scheduler suspended); the Next steps give the first line of the message, the full technical message is in the log. For a suspended scheduler: run Set-ADSyncScheduler -SchedulerSuspended $false on the Entra Connect server, then the delta sync
The RSAT ActiveDirectory module is not installed on this server: ... the AD part was started on a server without the RSAT feature Active Directory module install the RSAT feature, or run the AD part on a server that has it do not convert again: run a delta sync on the Entra Connect server, then carry the package (or -Phase Cloud -Batch <id>) as the Next steps say
<account> is already converted by batch <id> (it is a remote mailbox now) a Convert was started again for an object that the batch <id> already converted nothing is converted. To finish that batch (sync + package) run the command given in the Next steps: -Action Convert -Phase AD -Mode Apply -Batch <id>
This batch has no AD proof (State file) ... cannot be finished from here -Phase AD -Batch on a batch that stopped before its first verified object (or a batch of an old version): no object of it is proven nothing is finished from here. Put back what the batch changed with -Action Recover -Batch <id> (Preview first), then run a new Convert
<n> object(s) of this batch were not converted by it (it stopped at its first error) (warning; the objects are Skipped) -Phase AD -Batch or -Phase Cloud -Batch of a partial batch: its AD proof lists only the objects verified before the first error the converted objects are continued. For the others: fix the cause, then run a new Convert for those objects only (with -CsvPath, list only them), or roll the batch back (-Action Recover -Batch <id>, Preview first). The Next steps give the commands
Convert batch <id> cannot be resumed: Recover batch <id> already rolled back objects of it -Phase AD -Batch or -Phase Cloud -Batch on a Convert batch that a Recover already rolled back nothing is changed. To convert objects again, start a new Convert; to see what the rollback left, -Action Check -Batch <recover id> -Expect Deprovisioned
Stopped at step ...: the run was interrupted before it finished (Ctrl+C, a closed window or a stop of the host) (RESULT: FAIL, exit code 1) the run was stopped from outside read the Next steps: they continue the batch (or say how to undo it); what the run did is kept
<mailbox>: <n> shared mailbox permission(s) not granted by the settings ... - to grant by hand: FullAccess <user>; ... (warning, done with warnings) the batch carries permissions that the settings in force do not grant: a batch written before 3.2.0 on a server whose configuration grants less, or a batch converted with settings that grant none grant the listed permissions by hand (Add-MailboxPermission, Add-RecipientPermission, Set-Mailbox -GrantSendOnBehalfTo), or correct the settings and run the cloud phase again. Nothing else is wrong
The shared mailbox permission settings of this server differ from the ones of the batch (...) (warning) the cloud server has another SharedMailbox configuration than the server that converted nothing to do: the batch values are used, and the warning names them
<UPN>: the Microsoft Entra ID account with this UPN is not the account synchronised from this Active Directory object (it is a cloud-only account / it is synchronised from another Active Directory object) the UPN of the AD object belongs to another account in the cloud: Entra ID gave the synchronised object another UPN, or a cloud-only account had the UPN first nothing was changed on it, and nothing was read in Exchange Online. Give one of the two accounts another UPN so that Entra Connect synchronises the object under its own UPN, or leave the object out, then run the same command again. A record written by an older version says so: if the tenant uses another source anchor, check the account by hand and set Cloud.IdentityCheck = 'Off'
<UPN>: the Microsoft Entra ID account with this UPN is synchronised, but its onPremisesImmutableId ... the account is synchronised but carries another anchor than the objectGUID or ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid of the record, or one that is not the base64 of a GUID: the tenant may use another source anchor (a mail or employee attribute, for example) nothing was changed. Check by hand that the account is the one of the object, then set Cloud.IdentityCheck = 'Off' and run the same command again. Changing UPNs is not the answer here
<UPN>: Microsoft Graph refused to read the Microsoft Entra ID account that confirms this object (HTTP 403) the identity check needs User.Read.All and the sign-in does not have it give User.Read.All (delegated: the administrator consents; application: add it and grant admin consent), or set Cloud.IdentityCheck = 'Off'; run the same command again. Nothing was changed
<UPN>: Microsoft Graph did not accept the sign-in (HTTP 401): the sign-in expired or was refused the Graph sign-in expired during a long run, or the certificate or application was refused sign in again: run the same command again (a refusal of Graph, 401 or 403, stops the run once: ONE error, the objects not reached stay Pending, nothing is asked of Graph again)
The sign-out of Microsoft 365 failed (...) (warning) a session could not be closed at the end of the run what the run did is not affected, no object is an error; close a session that is still open with Disconnect-ExchangeOnline -Confirm:$false; Disconnect-MgGraph
<UPN>: a shared mailbox permission could not be granted or verified (...) the grant step failed (for example a throttled answer after the Add): it is never repeated in the same run run the cloud phase again later: it reads the permissions first and grants only what is missing
<UPN>: the account synchronised from this Active Directory object is <other UPN> in Microsoft Entra ID, not <UPN> the account of the object has another UPN in the cloud make the UPN in AD and in Entra ID the same, let Entra Connect synchronise, run the same command again
<UPN>: Microsoft Entra ID returned 2 accounts for this UPN / ... has 2 accounts that carry the source anchor of this Active Directory object duplicate accounts in Entra ID remove the duplicate account, run the same command again
Permissions on <shared mailbox> are not granted. <trustee>: the Microsoft Entra ID account ... a trustee of a permission is a cloud-only account or another account than the AD user nothing was granted for this mailbox. Fix the UPN of the trustee account as for an object, then run the same command again
The Exchange Online recipient / mailbox is not the Microsoft Entra ID account confirmed for this object: <UPN> Exchange Online returned another object than the account that was confirmed (the ExternalDirectoryObjectId differs) nothing was changed. Wait for Exchange Online to settle and run the same command again; if it stays, ask for the object in Exchange Online
<UPN>: the Microsoft Entra ID account is found by its UPN only: this object has no Active Directory identity in the record (warning) -Action Check -Identity <UPN> has no AD read give the sAMAccountName, or -Batch, to have the account confirmed

Measured durations: delta sync on the Entra Connect server (remote) about 5 min 30 s; cloud phase alone 28 s to 61 s once the objects are provisioned.

Defects found by the campaign and fixed in 2.0.0 (all now covered by the gate):

  1. With -Force, the approval callback of the AD engine still called ShouldProcess with ConfirmImpact High → "Windows PowerShell is in NonInteractive mode" in the scheduled task, before any write (fail-closed). Fix: the single confirmation of the run sets ConfirmPreference = None for the callbacks.
  2. The session guard compared the organisation domain of a certificate session with Cloud.TenantId and refused it (finding 1 of annex F). Fix: the guard accepts Cloud.Organization and checks the AppId.
  3. (T17) Get-EXORecipient -UserPrincipalName answers an absent object with HTTP 404 ManagementObjectNotFoundException. During the Recover cloud check, while the mailbox turns into a MailUser, this answer stopped the run (fail-closed). Fix: this exact answer, for this exact UPN, means "not there yet": the check waits and reads again; any other error still stops.
  4. (T18) A run that needs Microsoft Graph after a run that used Exchange Online in the same console failed with an obscure GetTokenAsync error. Fix: a clear message asks for a new Windows PowerShell window (annex A).
  5. (transcripts of T3 and T9) Before each FullAccess grant, the normal "No permissions were found" answer appeared as a TerminatingError line in the transcript. Fix: read through -ErrorVariable; T16 and T17c: 0 such line.

The lab was left as before the tests: T16 test material removed (groups deleted, msExchMailboxSecurityDescriptor identical to its copy taken before the test, publicDelegates empty), pra-shared03 back on-premises.

Lab fixes made before the campaign (outside the tool): domain controller DC2 had not replicated from DC1 since 2026-09-18 (Kerberos 0x80090322, stale KDC ticket); fixed by purging the tickets of the computer account and forcing the replication. Account LAB\pra-operator and the lab application (annex C) were created for the campaign.

3.0.0 has offline validation only (the gate, which replays the files written by the real 2.2.0 under Windows PowerShell 5.1: tests\PraLegacyFixtures.Tests.ps1, 23 checks on the fixtures frozen in tests\fixtures\ps51-2.2.0). Before any use in production, replay on the lab, with PowerShell 7.5+:

  1. Prerequisites on each lab server: pwsh 7.5+, RSAT ActiveDirectory (Get-Module ActiveDirectory -ListAvailable shows Core), ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.10+ and Microsoft.Graph 2.x installed for PowerShell 7, the application certificate reachable.
  2. Restoration of a real 2.2.0 history (acceptance test of the compatibility promise): Recover (AD phase, then cloud phase, then Finalize on two servers) of a Convert batch produced by 2.2.0 under Windows PowerShell 5.1 in the lab, and Check on that batch.
  3. Convert Preview and Apply, users and shared mailboxes (FullAccess, SendAs, SendOnBehalf); Recover; Retention / RestoreTag; Finalize.

Minimum permissions (chapter 4, What the code cannot tell you): with an account that is not a Domain Admin and holds only the dsacls delegation of chapter 4, run a Preview and an Apply on one user and one shared mailbox, then a Recover (if an attribute is refused, note which). With Directory.ForceReplication on, check that Replication synchronization alone is enough on every destination domain controller. Sign in to Graph with only the Entra role Exchange Recipient Administrator and run Check (a refusal of the licence read means a reader role such as Global Reader is needed). For each cmdlet of the Exchange Online table, Get-ManagementRoleEntry "*\<cmdlet>" and confirm the role. Certificate sign-in with a certificate created by the Annex C command (CSP provider) in CurrentUser\My.
Annex C

Certificate sign-in (application)

In short: How to sign in without a person: one application, one certificate, two permissions, one role.

Least privilege for unattended runs: one application, one certificate, two application permissions (User.Read.All for Microsoft Graph, Exchange.ManageAsApp for Exchange Online, both with admin consent) and one Entra role (Exchange Recipient Administrator) for its service principal. These are exactly the rows of the Certificate sign-in column of chapter 4, Permissions. The tool reads and grants nothing else through the application.

What the certificate must be (the console light Sign-in: Certificate checks the first three; Microsoft requires the last two for Exchange Online):

  • in the CurrentUser\My store of the account that runs the tool (the console light looks in this store only; a certificate that is only in LocalMachine\My shows a red light);
  • with its private key on this server;
  • not expired: renew it before the date shown in the light (valid until …); add the new certificate to the application before removing the old one;
  • created with a CSP key provider: a CNG key (the default of recent Windows) is refused by Exchange Online. The command below names the provider;
  • the .cer (public part) is uploaded to the application; the private key never leaves the server.
PowerShell
# 1. Certificate, in the store of the account that runs the tool (private key not exportable, CSP provider)
$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate -Subject 'CN=PRA Remote Mailbox' -CertStoreLocation Cert:\CurrentUser\My `
    -Provider 'Microsoft Enhanced RSA and AES Cryptographic Provider' `
    -KeyExportPolicy NonExportable -KeySpec Signature -KeyLength 2048 -HashAlgorithm SHA256 -NotAfter (Get-Date).AddYears(1)
Export-Certificate -Cert $cert -FilePath .\pra-app.cer
$cert.Thumbprint                                   # -> Cloud.CertificateThumbprint
PowerShell
# 2. Application (Azure CLI, Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator)
$app = az ad app create --display-name 'PRA Remote Mailbox' --sign-in-audience AzureADMyOrg --query appId -o tsv
az ad app credential reset --id $app --cert '@pra-app.cer' --append
$sp = az ad sp create --id $app --query id -o tsv
# Microsoft Graph: User.Read.All (application)
az ad app permission add --id $app --api 00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000 --api-permissions df021288-bdef-4463-88db-98f22de89214=Role
# Office 365 Exchange Online: Exchange.ManageAsApp (application)
az ad app permission add --id $app --api 00000002-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000 --api-permissions dc50a0fb-09a3-484d-be87-e023b12c6440=Role
az ad app permission admin-consent --id $app
# 3. Entra role Exchange Recipient Administrator for the service principal
az rest --method POST --url https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments `
    --body "{ \"roleDefinitionId\": \"31392ffb-586c-42d1-9346-e59415a2cc4e\", \"principalId\": \"$sp\", \"directoryScopeId\": \"/\" }"
$app                                               # -> Cloud.AppId

Note

With certificate sign-in, Exchange Online identifies the session by the organisation domain and the AppId: Cloud.Organization must be the initial domain (tenant.onmicrosoft.com) and Cloud.AppId the application ID. To revoke: delete the certificate credential of the application (or the application).

Warning

To validate in the lab. The -Provider parameter (CSP key, not CNG) follows Microsoft's requirement for app-only sign-in in Exchange Online; it was added to this command in 3.0.0 and has not been replayed on a tenant. The command of the earlier versions used the default provider. If Connect-ExchangeOnline refuses the certificate, recreate it with the provider named above. Whether the Entra role Exchange Recipient Administrator alone covers every cmdlet of chapter 4 is also a point to confirm once (chapter 4, What the code cannot tell you).

Annex D

File formats

In short: The formats of the files, so that old backups still restore.

File Format Key fields
Backup <Op>-<Env>-<date>-<id>.json schema 3 (schema 1 and 2 of 1.2.x/1.3.0-1.3.2 still read) Operation (Convert, Recover, Finalize), BatchId, Environment, Server, RawFile + RawHash, SourceBackupHash (Recover/Finalize: SHA-256 of the Convert backup), GrantSettings (Convert: Enabled, PermissionSource, GrantFullAccess, GrantSendAs, GrantSendOnBehalf in force at the Convert), Records[] (Attributes = before, PlannedAttributes = after, Licensing, Retention, SharedPermissions, CapturedUsnChanged)
Capture .clixml PraDataOnlyClixml-v1 every attribute returned by AD, closed descriptors (no native object)
AD proof State-<id>.json schema 2 Kind = ADVerified, BackupFile + BackupHash, Records[] (ObjectGuid, Operation, VerifiedUsnChanged); a Convert batch that stopped at its first error has Partial = true and PlannedCount (the number of objects planned), and lists only the objects verified
Journal Journal-<id>.jsonl (AD) and CloudOperations.jsonl (cloud phase, folder <RunId>-cloud, created after the confirmation) one JSON per line RunId, Utc, Target, Operation, Status, Detail. Statuses: Started, Applied, Verified (a write and its re-read), FailedOrIndeterminate (AD write failed or unknown), Failed (cloud write failed), Initialized (cloud journal opened, no cloud write yet), Completed (Entra Connect cycle finished)
Finalize package manifest schema 2, Operation = RecoverFinalize SourceBackupHash, StateHash, Items[] (RestoreShared, RestoreTag, DeprovisionConfirmed)

3.1.0 adds one optional field to each record of a Convert backup, ExpectedX500 (the X500 addresses to verify in Exchange Online); a backup without it is read as before.

3.2.0 adds two optional fields to each record of a Convert backup: SourceAnchor (ObjectGuid and ConsistencyGuid: the base64 onPremisesImmutableId texts of the object, ConsistencyGuid empty when the object has no ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid) and SharedTrusteeAnchors (for a shared mailbox, the anchors of each trustee by UPN, ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid first). SharedTrusteeAnchorsIncomplete (a boolean) is true when the schema could not be read for the trustees: a trustee then only has to be a synchronised account. A backup, batch or transfer package without them is read as before: the anchor is then derived from the ObjectGuid of the record (trustees: no anchor, a synchronised account is required).

An Apply that imports a transfer package also writes a small text file Backups\Imported\<batch id>.txt (the package name and the time), outside the batch folder. The console reads it to tell a batch imported on this server from one converted here: only the second is offered "finish it here" (AD part first), and only on a server that can run the AD part.

Every JSON has a .sha256 file; a mismatch is refused. Version 2.0.0 reads the batches of 1.3.x (tested: Recover of a 1.3.6 Convert batch in the lab).

The formats did not change in 3.0.0 (backup schema 3, PraDataOnlyClixml-v1, proof schema 2, Finalize manifest schema 2). The codec writes the same bytes under PowerShell 7 and under Windows PowerShell 5.1 (by design; tests\PraLegacyFixtures.Tests.ps1 replays, in the gate, backups, proofs and a Finalize package written by the real 2.2.0 under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and frozen in tests\fixtures\ps51-2.2.0), and every hash is a hash of the file bytes, so a backup, a proof or a Finalize package produced by 2.x is read, verified and restored by 3.0.0 without conversion. The JSON written by PowerShell 7 is formatted differently (2-space indentation, no Unicode escapes for the characters <, >, & and the apostrophe) but is the same JSON; 2.2.x reads it. One cosmetic difference in new files: the order of the multi-value lists is an ordinal sort (upper-case before lower-case, by UTF-16 code unit), where 2.x wrote the culture-aware order of Windows PowerShell 5.1; the comparisons sort both sides again, so no check depends on it. The CSV report keeps its UTF-8 BOM, as in 2.x.

Annex E

Versioning and upgrade from 1.3.6

In short: What changed between versions and how to upgrade.

From 2.x to 3.0.0. Install PowerShell 7.5+ and the AD, Exchange Online and Graph modules for PowerShell 7 (chapter 4); replace the package folder; keep Backups\ and the configuration file (same format; nothing to change); run the commands with pwsh (and change the action of scheduled tasks from powershell.exe to pwsh.exe, chapter 7). Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.4 are refused before any code runs. The 2.2.x package remains the Windows PowerShell 5.1 version and is the fallback on a server that cannot have PowerShell 7; both versions read the backups of the other.

  • One source: $script:ToolVersion in module\PRA.Common.psm1, exported as Get-PraToolVersion. The entry script (run context, report, audit, log), the window (title) and the package builder (tools\New-PraPackage.ps1, which reads that line as text) take the version from it. Nothing else in the code carries a version literal.
  • Literals that cannot be computed (the signature and the manifest hash the exact bytes, so a comment cannot be generated at run time). Change them together with the source, in the same commit; tests\PraRemoteMailbox.Tests.ps1 fails if one differs:
    • ModuleVersion of PraRemoteMailbox.psd1 (a test compares it with Get-PraToolVersion and with the top entry of CHANGELOG.md);
    • Version : x.y.z in the help .NOTES of Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1, PraRemoteMailbox.psm1, and in the header of module\PRA.Common.psm1, PRA.Directory.psm1, PRA.Backup.psm1, PRA.Cloud.psm1, PRA.Gui.psm1, PRA.Gui.Directory.ps1, config\PraRemoteMailbox.config.psd1 and templates\Report.template.html (signed or hashed files);
    • the sample banner in the help of Write-PraBanner (vx.y.z, PRA.Common.psm1) and the first line of PackageIntegrity.psd1 (comment, regenerated with the manifest);
    • version: in the front matter of this guide, and the generated docs\PraRemoteMailbox-Guide.html (rebuild it);
    • README.md (package and repository) and the CHANGELOG.md heading;
    • the repository-only headers Version of tools\New-PraPackage.ps1, tools\Build-Documentation.ps1, tests\Invoke-TestGate.ps1, tests\IntegrityFixture.ps1, tests\PackageIntegrity.Tests.ps1, tests\PraRemoteMailbox.Tests.ps1, tests\PraReport.Tests.ps1.
  • Release checklist: gate PASS · lab campaign (annex B) · pwsh tools\New-DocumentationImages.ps1 (PowerShell 7.5+, Microsoft Edge, documentation only: every picture of the README and the guides, then the two HTML guides) · owner signature and manifest (below) · tools\New-PraPackage.ps1 · git tag vX.Y.Z.
  • Signature and manifest after a change. Editing a signed or hashed file invalidates its signature or hash, and the package then refuses to start (by design). The owner (1) signs, with the timestamp, every PowerShell file of the inventory (Invoke-PraRemoteMailbox.ps1, PraRemoteMailbox.psd1, PraRemoteMailbox.psm1, module\PRA.Common.psm1, PRA.Directory.psm1, PRA.Backup.psm1, PRA.Cloud.psm1, PRA.Gui.psm1, PRA.Gui.Directory.ps1, Test-PackageIntegrity.ps1); (2) regenerates PackageIntegrity.psd1 with the SHA256 of every inventory file taken from the final signed bytes (the hash of a signed script includes its signature block, so it cannot be computed before signing), then signs the manifest; (3) runs the gate and tools\New-PraPackage.ps1. The gate and the Pester suites also pass on an unsigned working tree (the native-state tests accept the fail-closed state); tools\New-PraPackage.ps1 and the CI Package stage refuse an unsigned or changed source.

From 3.1.x to 3.2.0. The configuration file keeps working (new optional settings: Cloud.IdentityCheck, Cloud.RetryBudgetObjectSeconds, Cloud.RetryBudgetRunMinutes, Retention.CheckBeforeRecover and Retention.ProofMaxAgeHours). A Recover now checks retention first and stops when it is not covered: see the Retention section for -AcceptRetentionRisk and the retention proof of a two-server setup. 3.2.0 reads Microsoft Graph for every object, shared mailboxes and runs without a licence check included, to confirm the account of the object and of each trustee: the permission User.Read.All (delegated, with the consent of the signing-in administrator; or application, with admin consent) must therefore be in place for every run of the cloud part, not only for the licence checks. A refusal by Graph (403, insufficient privileges) stops the object with a message that names the permission. The alternative is Cloud.IdentityCheck = 'Off', which finds the accounts by UPN only and reads nothing for this purpose (a tenant whose source anchor is neither the objectGUID nor ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid needs it). Batches and backups of 3.1.x are read as before.

From 1.3.6: keep the old Backups folders; copy the values of DRP-Config.psd1 into the new file (same sections; ADConnect → EntraConnect; BackupFolder/LogFolder/ReportFolder → Storage/Logging/Report; Safety → Storage.ForbiddenBackupRoots); keep the same Environment to use the old batches. Command mapping: see CHANGELOG.md (table "Changed").

Annex F

Code review 2026-09-30

In short: The review of the code and what was fixed.

Review of version 1.3.6 (script 513 lines, four modules 3,386 lines, gate 325 tests) before the 2.0.0 rewrite.

# Finding Impact 2.0.0
1 Certificate sign-in to Exchange Online always refused by the session guard (TenantID of an app-only session = organisation domain) cloud phase impossible unattended; explains the "UnAuthorized" blocker of the 1.3.4 pilot fixed (annex C)
2 Missing ADSync detected after the AD writes batch half done (AD written, no sync, no cloud) — seen in the E2E pilot checked before the first write; remote sync added
3 One ShouldProcess prompt per AD write and per grant (ConfirmImpact High) dozens of prompts for a batch; operators used -Force blindly one confirmation after the plan
4 -BackupFile / -StateFile long paths, implicit choice of "the most recent backup" copy/paste errors (a line break in a path stopped a Recover on 09-09) short batch IDs, explicit, proof and source found automatically
5 Two modes that do the same thing (Inventory / Simulate), three ways to say "do not write" confusion Preview + -WhatIf
6 Settings read but ignored (WaitForSync, VerifyTrusteeInCloud), obsolete switches kept misleading configuration removed; unknown keys refused
7 Preview of a cloud phase reported missing permissions as errors and waited up to 60 min preview unusable before an Apply one pass, "to grant"
8 Console: every AD read and memory probe on screen, French/English mix, 358-character lines unreadable runs, hard to maintain compact console, English, details in the log
9 Two operator documents (guide + technical documentation, 210 KB) plus release notes and many session notes no single reference this guide
10 Exit code 0 for Pending an orchestrator cannot see that a next step is due exit code 2
11 Disconnect-ExchangeOnline message on stdout of the child process (subprocess mode) would break the one-line JSON protocol of the child output suppressed

No defect was found in the backup, receipt and proof engine; its logic is unchanged in 2.0.0 and covered by the gate.
